With S1983 (mlp4's content is irrelevant; a constant row costs the same 10.67), what attention 6 needs from position-4 activations is that they VARY.

THE_DAMAGE_CEILING_IS_10_7_NATS_S2004.claim: Context-free rows arriving at a live attention 6 cost about 10.7 nats, and it does not matter how many sites produce them. Compiling one MLP (mlp4) costs 10.669; two (mlp2+mlp3) 10.542; three (mlp2+3+4) 10.701; and S1981's below_mlp arm -- six compiled MLPs, layers 0-5 -- cost 10.688. Four configurations spanning one to six sites, all within 0.16 nats. Adding mlp2 and mlp3 on top of a compiled mlp4 costs 0.032 nats.
THE_DAMAGE_CEILING_IS_10_7_NATS_S2004.evidence: ops/does_the_repair_saturate.py, 51.2s, thirteen arms x three roles at 5,419, plus S1981's already-published below_mlp figure as an independent fourth point. pred_a True 3/3 (S2003's excess rebuilds within 0.01), pred_b True 3/3, pred_c FALSE 3/3. Derived controls True, all three reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_DAMAGE_CEILING_IS_10_7_NATS_S2004.open: If the ceiling is what a fully context-free input to attention 6 costs, any set containing mlp4 and no attention 5 or 6 should sit at it, and sets that reduce what reaches layer 6 should fall below -- S1981's below_all, which adds attention 0-5, measured 9.266, under the ceiling and unexplained by it.
THE_DAMAGE_CEILING_IS_10_7_NATS_S2004.pred_c_failed_because_its_model_did: It registered that the repair's super-additive excess would GROW with a third site. It collapses from +0.528 to -9.31, because the naive prediction it is measured against assumes single-site gains add, and once damage saturates they cannot. The excess statistic is meaningless above the ceiling, and S2003's +0.528 was measured just below it.
THE_DAMAGE_CEILING_IS_10_7_NATS_S2004.revises: S2003's explanation (not its measurements). Marked in that entry.

THE_FIX_HAS_A_DOMAIN_S2001.claim: Compiling attention 5 and 6 costs a FLAT ~0.65 nats and buys back an amount that grows with the compiled MLP's lone damage. It is worth +2.842 at mlp2 (lone 4.813) and +4.578 at mlp3 (lone 6.574), and a strict LOSS of 0.636 at mlp7 (lone 0.072), 0.657 at mlp6 (lone 0.202) and 0.241 at mlp5 (lone 2.022). The crossing lies between a lone damage of 2.02 and one of 4.81.
THE_FIX_HAS_A_DOMAIN_S2001.evidence: ops/where_the_fix_stops_paying.py, 49.6s, thirteen arms x three roles at 5,419. pred_a True 3/3, pred_b True 3/3, pred_c FALSE on two of three roles. Derived controls True, all three reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_FIX_HAS_A_DOMAIN_S2001.mlp5_is_on_the_crossing: Its loss is 0.241, well under the 0.65 plateau, so the pair IS partially rescuing mlp5 -- recovering about 0.4 of the 0.65 it costs, and simply not enough.
THE_FIX_HAS_A_DOMAIN_S2001.open: No measured MLP lies between 2.02 and 4.81 nats of lone damage, so the crossing is bracketed but not located. mlp0 and mlp1 have never been measured at all -- the two remaining sites below the boundary. S2002 runs them.
THE_FIX_HAS_A_DOMAIN_S2001.pred_c_failed_and_the_failure_is_the_res: The bar was that the loss deepens as the site gets cheaper: gain(mlp7) < gain(mlp6) < gain(mlp5) < 0. It does not -- it SATURATES. mlp7 loses 0.636 and mlp6 loses 0.657, so the cheaper site loses slightly LESS, by 0.021 and 0.030 nats (skip1200 satisfies the ordering by 0.002 and is the one role that passes). For a site the pair cannot help, the loss is just the standalone cost of compiling attention 5 and 6 -- 0.62 to 0.70 nats -- a constant, not a function of the site.
THE_FIX_HAS_A_DOMAIN_S2001.scopes: S1985's framing 'a compiled site is safe when...' was describing the upper half of this curve and quietly assuming every site was in it.

THE_FREQUENCY_AXIS_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_IN.claim: On the unseen-target bucket the sign structure is exactly preserved between coverages -- table raise positive on skip7000 and skip11000, negative at skip1200; converged build losing only at skip1200 -- where S2031 found the sign FLIPPING on the uncovered-input axis between the same two coverages. But the size collapses: skip1200's deficit goes -3.948 -> -0.386, a tenfold reduction (tables -2.318 -> -0.219, map cut -1.642 -> -0.167), while the two winning roles nearly double (+2.060 -> +3.830, +2.963 -> +3.945).
THE_FREQUENCY_AXIS_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_IN.evidence: ops/the_unseen_bucket_at_high_coverage.py, 5.8s warm, six arms x three roles at 16,110, written fresh rather than derived (LESSON 105). pred_a/b/c True, pred_d FALSE. Derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000, no crashed predicates.
THE_FREQUENCY_AXIS_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_IN.open: Both axes, both coverages and the price under both rules are measured. Every remaining question about this build is a DECISION rather than a measurement: S1947's rule (pooled versus concentrated cost) and S1979's architectural fork, both with Logan. The measurement frontier has moved back to BENCHMARK_BACKLOG rung 6, fresh-window certification, which S2028 recorded as unsatisfiable with the rowcaches on disk.
THE_FREQUENCY_AXIS_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_IN.pred_d_failed_against_S2031: I registered that the map cut's unseen-bucket tax would grow with coverage because S2031 measured exactly that on the uncovered-input axis (-0.9/-1.1 becoming -1.0/-1.8). On this bucket it SHRINKS on two roles of three (-0.855 -> -0.753, -1.642 -> -0.167), growing only at skip7000. Different cells, no contradiction, but the prediction that one would follow the other was wrong.
THE_FREQUENCY_AXIS_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_IN.what_S2029s_concern_amounts_to: The converged build's losses are real, concentrated in the uncovered arm and the unseen bucket, worst at the half-sized role, and they SHRINK with coverage -- the unseen-bucket deficit by a factor of ten. At the deployed 5,419 the exposure is what S2032 priced: 1.77M values and about 0.45 milli-nats separate the current build from the conservative one. S2035 does not change that number; it establishes that the number does not grow when the program is given more table.

THE_FREQUENCY_GRADIENT_IS_GENERIC_S1995.claim: S1994's 3:1 target-frequency gradient is a property of compiling ANYTHING, not of attention 6. The ratio of damage in the most frequent bucket to damage in the unseen bucket is 0.41-0.45 for mlp2+attention 5,6; 0.39 for mlp2+attention 5; 0.29 for a lone mlp2; 0.21-0.23 for a lone mlp4; 0.27 for the full 36-site program -- all clustered around the threshold gap's 0.29, though total damage across those arms differs by a factor of 2.2.
THE_FREQUENCY_GRADIENT_IS_GENERIC_S1995.evidence: ops/is_the_frequency_gradient_generic.py, 4.5s warm, six arms x three roles at 5,419. pred_a/b/c all True, derived controls True, all three reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_FREQUENCY_GRADIENT_IS_GENERIC_S1995.open: The threshold itself remains unexplained. The cheapest unasked question is one of DEGREE rather than membership: how much of attention 6 does it take? S1996 sweeps attention 6's table rank from 16 to 384 with everything else fixed, using per-site table ranks added to bqlib for it.
THE_FREQUENCY_GRADIENT_IS_GENERIC_S1995.status: CERTIFIED as a NEGATIVE. The observation in S1994 stands; the mechanism lead does not.
THE_FREQUENCY_GRADIENT_IS_GENERIC_S1995.why_it_matters: This is the control S1986, S1990 and S1992 did not get. Each of those was a shape that fit every number available, published as a rule, and falsified within the hour. S1994's gradient was registered as an OBSERVATION and its control was queued in the same commit -- 4.5 seconds, and the story died before it reached the board.

THE_FRESH_LOSS_IS_IN_THE_COVERED_ROWS_S2.claim: S2020's table raise loses on the fresh window in the COVERED rows: -17.432 milli-nats at 5,419 (150.6% of the -11.578 total, the uncovered arm gaining +0.943 and partially offsetting) and -37.845 at 16,110 (115.8% of -32.688, uncovered -4.433). S2029 measured the same change's IN-SAMPLE gain at covered inputs as +4.970/+4.787/+3.329. Same mechanism, same cells, opposite sign, three to eight times larger.
THE_FRESH_LOSS_IS_IN_THE_COVERED_ROWS_S2.evidence: ops/where_the_fresh_loss_lives.py, 9.2s warm, four arms on the fresh role at both coverages. All four predicates True, derived controls True, no crashed predicates.
THE_FRESH_LOSS_IS_IN_THE_COVERED_ROWS_S2.explains_the_coverage_growth: More coverage means more positions served by the covered tables; the covered harm grows -17.432 -> -37.845 while the fraction of positions in that arm rises. S2044's 2.8x is the covered arm getting larger, not the effect changing character.
THE_FRESH_LOSS_IS_IN_THE_COVERED_ROWS_S2.open: Not a measurement. The parameter space is closed: S1959's build, 189.5M, every parameter either validated out-of-sample or shown to sit in a flat region. What remains are S1947's price rule and S1979's architectural fork, both with Logan, and BENCHMARK_BACKLOG rung 4 (deploy gap) which has zero completions and zero ledger mentions.
THE_FRESH_LOSS_IS_IN_THE_COVERED_ROWS_S2.status: CERTIFIED. Closes the account of what S2020 did.
THE_FRESH_LOSS_IS_IN_THE_COVERED_ROWS_S2.the_retraction_line_complete: S2037 found it, S2038 attributed it to one axis, S2039 measured every depth, S2041 showed the restored ancestry survives, S2042-S2043 showed the last free parameter unidentifiable, S2044 validated the instrument at a second coverage, S2045 located the harm in the cells that had carried the gain. Nine sections to retract nineteen.

THE_FRESH_WINDOW_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_S204.claim: The held-out window gives the same verdict at both coverages and the central finding is stronger at the second. At 16,110 the converged build loses to S1959's by 32.650 milli-nats (t = -57.16) against 11.770 at 5,419; S2038's attribution holds exactly, the table raise alone accounting for -32.687 of the -32.650 total; and S1959 still beats S1789's deployed design by +98.768 (t = +40.90) against +127.889.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_S204.evidence: ops/is_the_fresh_window_itself_coverage_stable.py, 344.8s, six arms on the fresh role at 16,110. All four predicates True, derived controls True, no crashed predicates. pred_d passed narrowly: the bar allowed a factor of three and the actual ratio is 2.77.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_S204.open: S2029 decomposed the IN-SAMPLE loss into covered and uncovered arms and found the gain concentrated at covered inputs. The fresh-window loss has never been decomposed the same way. If the harm is in the covered rows, that explains the coverage growth and closes the account of what S2020 actually did.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_S204.status: CERTIFIED. Validates the instrument S2037-S2043 rest on.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_S204.the_growth_is_a_finding: The table raise hurts 2.8x more when the program has three times the coverage. More coverage means more positions served by the covered tables, which is exactly what untruncating changes.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_IS_COVERAGE_STABLE_S204.why_it_matters: S2037-S2043 rested on one held-out row set at one coverage. They now rest on that row set at two coverages with the central finding stronger at the second, where the retracted arc's own margins had the opposite property -- growing in-sample and reversing out. The retraction is not coverage-contingent.

THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.claim: On 98,304 fresh positions the alpha curve is unimodal with its peak at 0.40, beating the shipped 0.30 by +1.744 milli-nats at t = +3.42. Flanks: 0.10 -34.213 (t -27.03), 0.20 -9.673 (t -17.06), 0.50 -1.321 (t -1.38), 0.60 -8.262 (t -6.10), 0.70 -18.937 (t -11.02).
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.evidence: ops/sweep_alpha_on_fresh_rows.py, 4.4s warm, nine arms on the fresh role at 5,419. All four predicates True, derived controls True, no crashed predicates in the scored run.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.open: Score alpha 0.40 on the three original roles. They did not select it -- S2027's grid stopped at 0.36 -- so for that value they are an out-of-sample set. If 0.40 wins there too it wins on both row sets and neither selected it; if it loses, 0.30 stands and the fresh peak was selection.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.sensitive_and_flat_are_both_true: S2026 called alpha the most sensitive parameter and S1967's rule called it flat near the optimum. Both hold and are about different things: the flanks are brutal (0.10 costs 34 milli-nats, 0.70 costs 19) while the interval 0.28 to 0.50 spans about 3 milli-nats total -- the same scale as every quantity S2037 showed does not transfer. The build is not sensitive to alpha near its optimum, which is why two row sets can disagree about where it is.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.status: CERTIFIED as a measurement. NOT ADOPTED.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.the_row_sets_disagree: S2027's in-sample grid declines above 0.28 (+0.003082 at 0.28, +0.003064 at 0.30, +0.002852 at 0.32, +0.001895 at 0.36), so in-sample evidence puts the optimum at 0.28-0.30 and would put 0.40 lower still. The fresh window puts it at 0.40. Neither row set can certify the other's choice. Alpha 0.30 sits between the two optima, which is the honest reason to leave it there rather than a demonstration that it is best.
THE_FRESH_WINDOW_PREFERS_ALPHA_040_S2042.why_not_adopted: 0.40 was selected by looking at the fresh window. Adopting it on the strength of that window is exactly what S2013-S2035 did with the three published roles, and +1.744 milli-nats is about 0.05% of the build's ~3,300-milli-nat distance from the live model -- inside the regime LESSON 106 says is not a result until measured somewhere else. LESSON 106 applied to the agent one section after writing it.

THE_GAIN_IS_CONCENTRATED_AT_COVERED_INPU.SUSPECT_WAS_PARTLY_WRONG_S2030: S2029 named S2024's map cut as 'the suspect' for the uncovered-input deficit. S2030 attributes it: the map cut costs -0.868 to -1.067 milli-nats at uncovered inputs on every role and exactly 0.000 at covered ones -- uniform and mechanism-consistent. But at skip1200, the role with by far the largest deficit (-4.693), S2020's TABLE RAISE contributes -3.837, four times the map cut's -0.868. On the other two roles the table raise is positive at uncovered inputs. The map cut is the uniform cost; the table raise is the large one, and only on one role.
THE_GAIN_IS_CONCENTRATED_AT_COVERED_INPU.bears_on_a_question_with_logan: S1947's rule prices parameters against POOLED CE. S2023 and S2024 used it to sell parameters, and S2029 shows that sale's cost is concentrated in the weakest cells. Whether a price rule stated on an average may authorise a trade whose cost is not average is a decision about S1947.
THE_GAIN_IS_CONCENTRATED_AT_COVERED_INPU.claim: The converged build's advantage over S1959's is entirely at covered inputs and it is a net LOSS at uncovered ones on all three roles: covered +4.970/+4.787/+3.329 milli-nats, uncovered -0.734/-0.790/-4.693. It also loses the unseen-target bucket at skip1200 by 3.948. The pooled +3.064 S2028 recorded is the net of a larger gain and a real loss.
THE_GAIN_IS_CONCENTRATED_AT_COVERED_INPU.evidence: ops/where_does_the_converged_build_win.py, 4.3s warm, five arms x three roles at 5,419, using S1789's frequency buckets and S1936's covered/uncovered axis. pred_a True, pred_d True; pred_b FALSE 2 of 3, pred_c FALSE 0 of 3. Derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000, no crashed predicates.
THE_GAIN_IS_CONCENTRATED_AT_COVERED_INPU.named_suspect_not_yet_attributed: S2024 cut the map from rank 640 to 256 at MLP layers 0-7 and recorded it as net +0.47 milli-nats of budget under S1947's price rule -- a SALE of parameters priced on a pooled average. The map acts ONLY on uncovered rows. S2020's table ranks act on covered rows too, so they are not the obvious cause, but the loss has NOT been attributed and S2029 does not assert which change caused it. S2030 tests it.
THE_GAIN_IS_CONCENTRATED_AT_COVERED_INPU.not_a_frequency_effect: pred_a and pred_d passed -- all five frequency buckets gain on >=2 roles and the unseen bucket carries at least a fifth of the frequent bucket's win. The concentration is on the COVERED/UNCOVERED axis, not the frequency axis, which is the opposite of what pred_d was registered to look for.

THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.claim: mlp2's entire table content inside the shipped 36-site program is worth about 0.0003 nats -- the mean row is 0.00012 BETTER than the full-rank table at skip7000 and skip1200 -- against 1.408 nats for the same site's content in S2012's three-site repaired arm. Per S1515 no ratio is quoted: the denominator is within noise and the share is unbounded.
THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.evidence: ops/does_it_transfer_to_the_shipped_program.py, 92.9s, nine arms x three roles at 5,419, on the second plan (the first had no same-spec pair and control_is_two_sided FAILED). pred_a/b/c all True 3/3, derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000.
THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.mechanism: Structural, and it follows from S1765. In the fully compiled program every module's output is a fixed per-token row, so NOTHING DOWNSTREAM READS mlp2's output -- it contributes only its own additive term to the residual stream. S2012's 1.408 nats were entirely about live downstream attention, which the shipped program does not have.
THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.open: The mechanism predicts the fully compiled program's cost is ADDITIVE over sites, since each contributes an independent residual term. S1981 measured badly non-additive costs but every arm there had LIVE attention. In the shipped frame the prediction is exact additivity and it is cheap to falsify. S2014 runs it.
THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.shippable_corollary: Dropping mlp2 from rank 768 to rank 128 costs 0.00025 nats at pooled t = +8.97 -- real, and far under S1947's 0.010-per-100M bar. The parameters saved are 4.2M at that one site, worth 0.00042 nats at that price. Rank 128 at mlp2 is marginally justified, by 0.0002 nats, at one site of eighteen. S1947 and S1959 swept the MLP rank uniformly and jointly with attention; a per-site allocation has never been priced.
THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.status: CERTIFIED, and it BOUNDS the S1983-S2012 arc.
THE_LOCALISATION_LINE_DOES_NOT_REACH_THE.the_boundary: Fourteen sections localised a penalty that exists only when attention is alive. The shipped program has no interface to break, no ceiling, no lever and no threshold. Everything from the ceiling to attention 5's presence-only character is a statement about programs S1765 does not produce.

THE_MAP_CUT_PRICED_UNDER_BOTH_RULES_S203.claim: The two rules disagree and the disagreement is now quantified. Under S1947's pooled rule every cut depth is net-positive and deeper is strictly better: +0.260/+0.406/+0.472 milli-nats at 5,419 for cuts to layers 3/5/7, and +0.319/+0.485/+0.573 at 16,110. Under an uncovered-arm view the same choice costs 0.86-1.05 milli-nats where a stop at layer 5 costs 0.40-0.57. The tax per cut site varies by 2.2x across depths, so a partial cut can be priced by interpolation, but the MARGINAL structure is sharper: layers 0-5 cost about 0.082 per site in the uncovered arm and layers 6-7 about 0.226 -- 2.8x more.
THE_MAP_CUT_PRICED_UNDER_BOTH_RULES_S203.evidence: ops/price_the_map_cut_against_both_rules.py, 9.7s warm, seven arms x three roles x two coverages. pred_a/b/c True, pred_d FALSE by 0.007 milli-nats. Derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000, no crashed predicates.
THE_MAP_CUT_PRICED_UNDER_BOTH_RULES_S203.open: S2029 also found the converged build losing the UNSEEN-TARGET bucket at skip1200 by 3.948 milli-nats, and S2030/S2031 attributed the coverage axis without decomposing the frequency axis. Which of the two changes loses that bucket has not been measured, and it is the one cell the fallback exists to serve.
THE_MAP_CUT_PRICED_UNDER_BOTH_RULES_S203.pred_d_missed_by_0_007: The bar was that cutting only layers 0-5 costs under HALF the full cut's pooled CE. It costs 0.125 against 0.236, a ratio of 0.53, where half of 0.236 is 0.118. The partial reversal is still available; it does not clear the bar as written.
THE_MAP_CUT_PRICED_UNDER_BOTH_RULES_S203.status: CERTIFIED. This is the decision table; no further run is needed to choose.
THE_MAP_CUT_PRICED_UNDER_BOTH_RULES_S203.the_decision: If S1947's pooled rule stands as written: cut layers 0-7, which is the current build, +0.472 milli-nats of budget at 5,419. If the uncovered arm is to be protected: cut layers 0-5, keep 75% of the released values, pay 48% of the uncovered tax. The difference between the two builds is 1.77M values and about 0.45 milli-nats in the uncovered arm. That is the whole exposure and it is small.

THE_MAP_CUT_TAX_IS_STABLE_THE_TABLE_RAIS.claim: At 16,110 the map cut costs -1.282/-1.791/-1.024 milli-nats at uncovered inputs and EXACTLY 0.000 at covered ones -- six cells across two coverages, six zeros -- and its cost GROWS with coverage, the wrong direction for a fallback whose uncovered arm has halved. S2020's table raise gives +1.498/-1.869/-3.655 at uncovered inputs against +0.316/+0.130/-3.837 at 5,419: the sign flips at skip11000 and only one role is positive. Covered gains nearly double at the higher coverage (+8.811/+9.247/+6.691 against +4.970/+4.787/+3.329).
THE_MAP_CUT_TAX_IS_STABLE_THE_TABLE_RAIS.evidence: ops/uncovered_cost_at_high_coverage.py, 5.8s warm, six arms x three roles at 16,110. pred_a/b/d True, pred_c FALSE. Derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000, no crashed predicates.
THE_MAP_CUT_TAX_IS_STABLE_THE_TABLE_RAIS.my_registered_dichotomy_was_unanswerable: I asked whether skip1200's deficit is a property of the ROLE or of the uncovered arm's SIZE. skip1200 barely moves (-3.837 -> -3.655) when the arm halves, which says role; skip11000 moves 2.0 milli-nats and changes sign, which says the question was wrong for the other roles. The data support neither branch cleanly and neither is claimed. pred_a passed on the narrowest margin in the run: skip1200's two figures differ by 0.091 against a 0.05 bar.
THE_MAP_CUT_TAX_IS_STABLE_THE_TABLE_RAIS.open: S1947's rule cannot see either: it prices against pooled CE, and one change has a concentrated cost the pool hides while the other has an unstable one the pool averages away. That is with Logan. Available without him: the map cut is reversible for 7.08M values, and S2024's ladder says layers 0-5 cost 0.24x where 6-7 cost 0.63x, so a partial reversal exists and has never been priced against the uncovered arm specifically.
THE_MAP_CUT_TAX_IS_STABLE_THE_TABLE_RAIS.what_survives: The map cut is a uniform, mechanism-exact ~1-1.8 milli-nat tax on the uncovered arm and zero elsewhere, at both coverages, bought for 7.08M values worth 0.71 milli-nats pooled. The table raise is a large covered-input gain whose uncovered side is unstable in both sign and size. Two different kinds of change, priced by S2028 with one rule.

THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.REFINED_BY_S2024: S2023 stopped the cut at layer 5 on a four-site average. S2024's per-two-site ladder shows layers 6 and 7 are also free (0.59x and 0.66x) and layers 8-9 are not (2.85x). The cut runs to layer 7: 7.08M released worth 0.71 milli-nats for a 0.236 CE cost, net +0.47 against S2023's +0.40. Build 204.4M -> 202.6M.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.RETRACTED_BY_S2037: RETRACTED BY S2037. On a fresh window (512 rows, 98,304 positions, zero overlap with any fit or eval set) the converged build LOSES to S1959's by 11.770 milli-nats at t = -28.71, against +3.064 in-sample. The measurements stand; the build they compose into is worse than the one it replaced. Build of record reverts to S1959's: {mlp 768, attn 384}, 30% neighbour / 70% rank-640 map, 189.5M values.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.S2038_OUT_OF_SAMPLE: MEASUREMENT CONFIRMED OUT-OF-SAMPLE by S2038: the map cut's CE cost is -0.206 milli-nats on fresh rows against -0.236 in-sample, same sign and order, t = -4.50. It was never a fitted quantity. What remains open is not whether the cost is real but whether releasing 7.08M values is worth paying it -- the S1947 question, now on out-of-sample evidence.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.build: 36 tables at {attn 384; mlp 768 at layers 0-9, mlp 1152 at layers 10-17}; uncovered rows 30% output-NN neighbour, 70% map at rank 640 EXCEPT rank 256 at MLP layers 0-5. 204.4M values at 5,419, down from 209.7M (-2.5%). CE is 0.125 milli-nats WORSE; the 5.31M released are worth 0.53 at S1947's price; net +0.40 milli-nats of budget.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.claim: S1870's map is over-bought at the shallow MLP sites. Cutting it from rank 640 to 256 costs 0.000125 nats at MLP layers 0-5 against 0.00053 of released parameters (0.24x at 5,419, 0.09x at 16,110); 0.000740 at layers 0-9 against 0.00089 (0.83x / 0.31x); and 0.007423 at all eighteen against 0.00160 (4.64x / 1.66x). S1959's map turnover at 640 is correctly placed for the sites that need it.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.codex_scopes_the_layer_10_knee: Codex's exact polarization-slice certificate finds all MLP0-17 slices at numerical rank 1152 with SMOOTH rank-768 coefficient tails: MLP10/MLP9 = 1.0113x and the median of MLP10-17 over MLP0-9 = 1.0554x, both failing their frozen 1.20x knee rule. So S2020's layer-10 knee is not a property of the model's coefficient structure -- it is a property of what the compiled program's economics ask of each site. A sharper statement than S2021 could make from CE alone.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.evidence: ops/does_the_map_want_per_site_rank.py, 213.4s, seven arms x three roles x two coverages, all figures pooled over 92,160 positions, using composite arms to give different sites different map ranks. pred_a/b/c/d all True, derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.open: The map knee is bracketed between layers 5 and 9 by a step averaging four sites. S2015's content profile is an order of magnitude apart inside that bracket (mlp6 0.00012, mlp8 0.00138), so the knee may sit within it. S2024 halves the bracket.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.status: RETRACTED as a build recommendation by S2037; measurements stand.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.the_marginal_rule_cuts_less_than_the_blo: Layers 0-5 cost 0.24x; the increment from there to 0-9 -- four more sites, 3.54M, worth 0.36 milli-nats -- costs 0.615, a 1.71x LOSS. The block ratio of 0.83x hides a marginal ratio of 1.71x, so the cut stops at layer 5.
THE_MAP_IS_OVER_BOUGHT_AT_SHALLOW_SITES_.what_kind_of_result_this_is: Every supersession from S2018 to S2020 bought CE with parameters. S2023 sells parameters for CE at a favourable rate, which the price rule sanctions and this ledger has never done. If the rule is meant only to justify purchases and not sales, that is a decision about S1947 rather than about this measurement. The CE number is unambiguously worse and is not hidden behind the ratio.

THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.PRED_D_WAS_A_CRASH_CORRECTED_S2026: When S2024 was written, pred_d had NOT been evaluated: it raised KeyError('cut7','shipped') and run() recorded the crash as False, printing it identically to a measured negative. THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.RETRACTED_BY_S2037: RETRACTED BY S2037. THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.S2038_OUT_OF_SAMPLE: MEASUREMENT CONFIRMED OUT-OF-SAMPLE by S2038: the map cut's CE cost is -0.206 milli-nats on fresh rows against -0.236 in-sample, same sign and order, t = -4.50. THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.claim: At the deployed 5,419 coverage the rank-256 map cut runs to MLP layer 7 and stops at 8: per-two-site costs are 0.18x, 0.59x, 0.66x through layer 7 and 2.85x at layers 8-9. At 16,110 NO step fails -- layers 8-9 cost 0.78x, still free -- so the knee is at layer 8 at one coverage and beyond layer 9 at the other.

THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.first_parameter_where_the_coverages_disa: The map acts only on uncovered rows and 16,110 halves that arm, so a poorer map costs less there; the knee moving outward with coverage is the expected direction. S1960 asked this for the allocation and found one build within 0.002 nats of both optima; the map cut is the first parameter where that no longer holds. The disagreement is 1.8M values -- small, but a disagreement rather than a shared optimum. The deployed coverage is 5,419 and that is the build recorded.
THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.open: Every knee found since S2020 -- table rank at layer 10, map rank at layer 8 -- sits mid-stack with no native explanation (Codex's certificate, S2023). THE_MAP_KNEE_IS_COVERAGE_DEPENDENT_S2024.status: RETRACTED as a build recommendation by S2037; measurements stand.

THE_MINIMAL_PATH_IS_THREE_SITES_S1990.WITHDRAWN_RULE_NOTE: S1991 falsifies the RULE'S FORM, not S1990's measurements. The 'every attention layer strictly above the compiled site' statement was derived from one site and cannot distinguish a chain from its endpoint. S1991 removed attention 3 from mlp2's path (mlp2+attn4-6 = 1.845) and it got BETTER than the unbroken version (mlp2+attn3-6 = 1.887) by 0.042 nats at pooled t = +18.9. There is no chain. What every working arm shares is attention 5 and attention 6. S1990's numbers stand and reproduced to 0.000000 in S1991.
THE_MINIMAL_PATH_IS_THREE_SITES_S1990.claim: The minimal path is THREE SITES: mlp4 + attention 5 + attention 6, at 1.555/1.640/1.498 nats -- 99.6% of the lone-mlp4 penalty (10.669) removed, and 1.25 nats BELOW the full 36-site program. Attention 4 runs before mlp4 in block order and was never in the path: dropping it is worth 0.198 nats at pooled t = -239.5. Neither remaining layer works alone -- attention 5 alone leaves 8.021, attention 6 alone leaves 10.666, the pair gives 1.555 (-6.543 at t = -344.2 and -9.178 at t = -371.9).
THE_MINIMAL_PATH_IS_THREE_SITES_S1990.evidence: ops/the_minimal_path.py, 47.5s, seven arms x three roles at 5,419. pred_a/b/c all True, derived controls True, all three reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_MINIMAL_PATH_IS_THREE_SITES_S1990.open: The rule was derived from one site. It predicts mlp2's minimal path is attention 3-6, and that dropping attention 3 as well breaks it. S1987 bought attention 2-6 without asking. S1991 tests it.
THE_MINIMAL_PATH_IS_THREE_SITES_S1990.still_probes: Three compiled sites score better than thirty-six partly because thirty-three more of the live model is present. Evidence about where the penalty lives, not a program. The S1979 architectural fork is unchanged.
THE_MINIMAL_PATH_IS_THREE_SITES_S1990.the_rule_WITHDRAWN_BY_S1991: A compiled site is safe when every attention layer STRICTLY ABOVE it, up to and including attention 6, is also compiled -- and nothing else is. Sites below it cost (S1986 -0.372, S1990 -0.198). A path stopped short costs more than no path (S1987 +2.08). Above attention 6 nothing is required (S1988/S1989: 0.03-0.20 nats). The site that matters is mlp4, its content is irrelevant (S1983), and S1978's whole 3.6x partial-compilation penalty is one chain: mlp4 -> attention 5 -> attention 6.

THE_PREMISE_COSTS_2P7_NATS_S1977.claim: S1765's 36-site substitution costs 2.63 to 2.98 nats against the live model. The entire S1946-S1976 arc recovered 0.069 nats -- 2.4% of it. The fallback lever is worth 0.072 and coverage 0.074; the marginal parameters of S1957-S1974 are worth 0.001-0.005 each. Everything optimised since S1946 lives in the last 2.5% of the gap the premise opens.
THE_PREMISE_COSTS_2P7_NATS_S1977.method_note: Six numbers already sitting in an artifact written two hours earlier for a different purpose. The ce_live column has been carried in every cells() payload since S1936 as a CONTROL, and it answered the arc's largest open question at zero cost. Recording the control alongside the result rather than a pass/fail on it is what made that possible -- the same property that let S1974 re-read 190 comparisons under a new instrument.
THE_PREMISE_COSTS_2P7_NATS_S1977.not_a_criticism: S1946-S1976 optimised WITHIN the premise and did it well -- 18% cheaper and 69 milli-nats better than the deployed design with every axis settled under a stated criterion. This is a proportion the ledger did not contain, and it says a next order of magnitude would have to come from relaxing S1765 itself -- letting some sites see context again -- which no section since S1746 has tried to price.
THE_PREMISE_COSTS_2P7_NATS_S1977.open: Pricing a PARTIAL substitution -- restoring context to some sites and measuring what each is worth -- needs a `sites` parameter bqlib's row hook does not have: every arm substitutes all 36. A small library change, and the first experiment since S1946 that would ask what the compiled program is GIVING UP rather than how cheaply it can give it up.
THE_PREMISE_COSTS_2P7_NATS_S1977.status: CERTIFIED as a statement of proportion.
THE_PREMISE_COSTS_2P7_NATS_S1977.where_the_price_is: NOT the fallback. The COVERED arm -- positions where the program has an exact per-token table for the current token -- costs +2.57 to +2.89 nats, within 0.2 nats of the uncovered arm's +2.93 to +3.25. Having the right table is worth about 0.3 nats; having ATTENTION is worth about 2.7. S1936's covered/uncovered gap, which S1975 closed 40% of, is a tenth the size of the gap both arms share.

THE_RANK_KNEE_LOCATED_S2021.claim: S2020's build (MLP layers 10-17 untruncated) is CONFIRMED as the correct stopping point, not superseded. The marginal ladder, each step exactly two sites and 5.05M values at a 0.00050 price: sites 16,17 +0.000962 (1.9x); 14,15 +0.001170 (2.3x); 12,13 +0.000636 (1.3x); 10,11 +0.000531 (1.1x); 8,9 +0.000159 (0.3x). At 16,110: 4.7x / 4.7x / 4.0x / 1.9x / 0.6x. Under a marginal rule the ladder pays down to layers 10-11 and stops at 8-9, at both coverages.
THE_RANK_KNEE_LOCATED_S2021.evidence: ops/where_exactly_is_the_rank_knee.py, 545.1s, seven arms x three roles x two coverages, all gains pooled over 92,160 positions. pred_a/b/c/d all True, derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000.
THE_RANK_KNEE_LOCATED_S2021.marginal_rule_vs_ratio_maximising: The per-parameter champion is not the recommended build. Layers 14-17 alone return 2.1x per parameter against layers 10-17's 1.6x. S1947's rule is a MARGINAL rule, not a ratio-maximising one: buy every step that clears the bar. A ratio-maximising reading would stop at 14-17 and leave 1.2 milli-nats on the table. Recorded because the two give different builds and the ledger has never had to separate them.
THE_RANK_KNEE_LOCATED_S2021.open: Every rank finding since S2016 concerns the MLP sites. S1959 set ATTENTION at 384 by the same uniform sweep, averaging over eighteen attention sites whose lone contributions S1989 measured as differing by 6x. The attention rank axis above 384 has never been tested per-site -- same instrument, same failure mode. S2022 runs it.
THE_RANK_KNEE_LOCATED_S2021.the_knee_is_a_cliff_at_the_end_of_a_slop: pred_d passed -- layers 10-11 buy 3.34x what layers 8-9 buy, against a 3.0 bar -- but the fuller ladder shows the approach is a DECLINE, not a plateau: 1.9x, 2.3x, 1.3x, 1.1x, then 0.3x. S2020's 'sharp' was measured from one arm on each side.
THE_RANK_KNEE_LOCATED_S2021.the_two_profiles_do_not_track: S2015 measured what each table CARRIES: mlp14 0.0126, mlp12 0.0269, mlp10 0.0107, mlp8 0.0014. S2021 measures what MORE RANK buys: 0.00117, 0.00064, 0.00053, 0.00016. The content profile peaks at mlp12; the extra-rank profile peaks at mlp14-15 and declines monotonically. What a table holds and what a fuller table would add are different quantities and not even monotonically related -- precisely the conflation that produced S2020's wrong registered direction.

THE_RESTORED_BUILDS_ANCESTRY_HOLDS_S2041.build_of_record: S1959's: {mlp 768, attn 384}, uncovered rows 30% output-NN neighbour / 70% rank-640 map, 189.5M values. ONE parameter -- alpha against its high end -- rests on in-sample evidence only.

THE_RESTORED_BUILDS_ANCESTRY_HOLDS_S2041.evidence: ops/does_the_1959_build_survive_fresh.py, 194.3s, seven arms on the fresh role at 5,419. pred_a/b/c True, pred_d FALSE. Derived controls True, no crashed predicates.

THE_RESTORED_BUILDS_ANCESTRY_HOLDS_S2041.status: CERTIFIED. The retraction does not cascade.

THE_SHIPPED_PROGRAM_IS_SUPERADDITIVE_IN_.claim: Two findings. (1) Site relevance in the shipped 36-site program is NOT uniform: replacing a site's table with a mean row costs -0.00012/+0.00002/-0.00028 at mlp2 and -0.00020/-0.00016/-0.00075 at mlp3, but +0.02692/+0.02912/+0.02687 at mlp12 -- more than a hundred times either. (2) The program is NOT additive: degrading all three costs +0.03249/+0.03522/+0.03198 against a sum of +0.02661/+0.02898/+0.02584, super-additive by 22%.
THE_SHIPPED_PROGRAM_IS_SUPERADDITIVE_IN_.corrects_my_own_prediction: S2013 argued each site contributes an INDEPENDENT ADDITIVE TERM to the residual stream, and I predicted additive CE from it. That does not follow: the loss is a softmax cross-entropy of their sum, which is nonlinear, so independent perturbations compound. S2013's structural claim stands exactly as stated; the prediction I drew from it confused additivity of the computation with additivity of the objective. LESSON 100.
THE_SHIPPED_PROGRAM_IS_SUPERADDITIVE_IN_.evidence: ops/is_the_shipped_program_additive.py, 4.7s warm, seven arms x three roles at 5,419, on the second plan (the first paired two different composite arms as same-spec and inert_pairs_are_inert FAILED). pred_a True 3/3; pred_b FALSE by 0.022 on mlp12; pred_c FALSE by 0.0039/0.0042/0.0041. Derived controls True, reference deviation 0.000000.
THE_SHIPPED_PROGRAM_IS_SUPERADDITIVE_IN_.library_bug_found: Two DIFFERENT composite arms (meanrow@mlp2+... and meanrow@mlp3+...) shared rank, site set and whole-table flag, so inertness_pairs called them same-spec and asserted inertness between entirely different interventions. It failed, correctly. Only PLAIN arms, which differ solely in the fallback, may now be paired as inert; a test locks it.
THE_SHIPPED_PROGRAM_IS_SUPERADDITIVE_IN_.open: mlp12 is a hundred times more relevant than mlp2 in the shipped program, and no depth profile of that quantity exists. Every profile in this line (S1988, S2002) measured lone-compilation damage with attention LIVE, which S2013 showed is a different regime. The shipped program has its own depth profile and it has never been measured.
THE_SHIPPED_PROGRAM_IS_SUPERADDITIVE_IN_.scopes_S2013: S2013 measured mlp2 and generalised to 'a compiled site's content'. That was one site and the wrong one: mlp12 is worth 0.027 nats. The boundary S2013 drew -- that the S1983-S2012 arc is about live attention -- is unaffected.

THE_SPIKE_IS_MLP4_NOT_LAYER_4_S1989.claim: The spike belongs to mlp4, not to the residual stream at layer 4. A lone compiled attention 4 costs 0.288/0.279/0.308 nats against mlp4's 10.669/10.937/10.580 at the same depth -- pooled difference -10.471 at t = -396.4. Every lone attention layer below the boundary is cheap: attn2 0.179, attn3 0.113, attn4 0.288, attn5 0.241; attn7 above it 0.054.
THE_SPIKE_IS_MLP4_NOT_LAYER_4_S1989.evidence: ops/does_attention_spike_too.py, 60.5s, eight arms x three roles at 5,419. pred_a FALSE (attn4 at 0.288 against a 1.0-nat bar), pred_b True 3/3, pred_c True 3/3. Derived controls True, both reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_SPIKE_IS_MLP4_NOT_LAYER_4_S1989.open: In block order attention 4 runs BEFORE mlp4, so it sits below the compiled site, where S1986 found sites cost rather than help. S1986's four-site path probably carries a site it does not need; the minimal path should be mlp4 + attention 5 + attention 6. S1990 tests it.
THE_SPIKE_IS_MLP4_NOT_LAYER_4_S1989.the_shadow: The attention profile DOES peak at layer 4 -- attn4 beats attn5 by 0.044 at pooled t = +24.9 and attn2 by 0.097 at t = +46.6 -- but the whole attention profile is 37x smaller than the MLP one. The same shape, a faint shadow.
THE_SPIKE_IS_MLP4_NOT_LAYER_4_S1989.where_the_line_ends: Eight sections narrowed S1978's 3.6x partial-compilation penalty from 36 sites to ONE: mlp4, read by attention 6. Any attention layer alone costs 0.05-0.31; any MLP above attention 6 costs 0.03-0.20; mlp5 costs 2.02; mlp4 costs 10.67, and S1983 showed the row's content is irrelevant.

THE_SPLIT_TRANSFERS_IN_SIGN_NOT_SIZE_S19.claim: S1998's presence/content split second-class confirms at a different compiled MLP in SIGN ONLY. At mlp4 a mean row at attention 5 beats its compiled table by 0.017/0.017/0.020 nats (attention 5's content is negative at both sites) and a mean row at attention 6 costs +0.095/+0.098/+0.080 (positive at both). But at mlp2 the attention-6 figure is +0.212/+0.216/+0.191 -- roughly twice as much. How much attention 6 must carry is a fact about the pair, not about the layer.
THE_SPLIT_TRANSFERS_IN_SIGN_NOT_SIZE_S19.evidence: ops/the_split_at_mlp4.py, 51.0s, ten arms x three roles at 5,419, with both the mlp2 and mlp4 sides rebuilt in-run rather than one retyped. pred_a True 3/3; pred_b and pred_c both FALSE 3/3. Derived controls True, all three reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_SPLIT_TRANSFERS_IN_SIGN_NOT_SIZE_S19.open: Two sites give a difference but not a trend. Lone-site damages run mlp2 4.81, mlp3 6.57, mlp4 10.67, and attention 6's content is worth +0.21 at the first and +0.09 at the last -- the INVERSE order, not what 'more broken sites need more help' would predict. mlp3 is the one cheap point that would say whether this is monotone.
THE_SPLIT_TRANSFERS_IN_SIGN_NOT_SIZE_S19.status: CERTIFIED as a PARTIAL confirmation. The qualitative split stands; the magnitude claim does not.
THE_SPLIT_TRANSFERS_IN_SIGN_NOT_SIZE_S19.the_misses: pred_b's bar was 'a mean row at attention 6 still costs more than 0.10 nats at mlp4'. It costs 0.095/0.098/0.080 -- short by 0.005, 0.002 and 0.020, and the bar was set from the mlp2 figures. pred_c's bar was 'within 0.10 nats of the same quantity at mlp2'; the differences are 0.117/0.118/0.111, short by 0.011-0.018.

THE_TABLE_RAISE_IS_THE_WHOLE_FAILURE_S20.claim: On 98,304 fresh positions, S2020's table raise alone costs -11.578 milli-nats (t = -28.36) against +3.300 in-sample -- 98.4% of the composed deficit -- while S2024's map cut alone costs -0.206 against -0.236 in-sample (t = -4.50), reproducing in sign and order. The two components sum to -11.785 against a composed -11.770, a gap of 0.015: on fresh rows they are additive to a hundredth of a milli-nat, where S2014 measured the shipped program super-additive by 22% in-sample.
THE_TABLE_RAISE_IS_THE_WHOLE_FAILURE_S20.evidence: ops/does_any_finding_survive_fresh_rows.py, 177.3s, six arms on the fresh role at 5,419. All four predicates True, derived controls True, no crashed predicates.
THE_TABLE_RAISE_IS_THE_WHOLE_FAILURE_S20.narrows_S2037: S2020 is falsified out-of-sample. S2018 and S2019 raised subsets of the same eight sites and were not scored individually -- presumption, not measurement. S2023 and S2024's MEASUREMENTS are confirmed out-of-sample; only the S1947 trade remains open. S2028's retraction stands, since it certified the composition.
THE_TABLE_RAISE_IS_THE_WHOLE_FAILURE_S20.open: S2021's marginal ladder found the table raise paying down to layers 10-11 and stopping at 8-9, all in-sample. Whether ANY depth of untruncation survives fresh rows is one arm on the ladder that already exists.
THE_TABLE_RAISE_IS_THE_WHOLE_FAILURE_S20.the_pattern: The component that was SELECTED FOR -- fifteen sections of choosing a rank that maximised a margin -- reversed. The component that was MEASURED AND PAID FOR -- a cost accepted in exchange for parameters, never optimised -- reproduced. Selection is what failed to travel, not measurement.

THE_TILT_REJECTION_TRANSPORTS_IN_SHAPE_N.claim: On the fresh window flat alpha beats every tilt and the ordering is exactly monotone in tilt span -- 28->32 -0.123 (t -1.95), 25->35 -0.502 (t -3.19), 22->38 -1.128 (t -4.48), 20->40 -1.688 (t -5.37), 15->45 -3.620 (t -7.73), 10->50 -6.373 (t -10.30) -- matching the shape S1967 measured in-sample. But the best tilt's deficit is 15.6x smaller than S1967's 1.92 milli-nats, and the narrowest tilt is inside the noise band at t = -1.95.
THE_TILT_REJECTION_TRANSPORTS_IN_SHAPE_N.evidence: ops/was_the_tilt_rejected_on_selection.py, 123.4s, nine arms on the fresh role at 5,419. pred_a/c True, pred_b/d FALSE. Derived controls True, no crashed predicates.
THE_TILT_REJECTION_TRANSPORTS_IN_SHAPE_N.open: S2046's audit left thirteen in-sample selections standing; the tilt family is now three of them. The largest remaining is S1960's 'one build suffices' -- a single build within 0.002 nats of the coverage-specific optimum at both coverages, decided on a 3.0 milli-nat margin. S2024 already found one parameter where the two coverages disagree.
THE_TILT_REJECTION_TRANSPORTS_IN_SHAPE_N.status: CERTIFIED. S1964 and S1967's rejection of the tilt FAMILY is confirmed out-of-sample; the last grid step of it is not.
THE_TILT_REJECTION_TRANSPORTS_IN_SHAPE_N.the_structural_contrast: On fresh rows the untruncation depths SCRAMBLED (-10.371, -6.006, -5.777, -11.578 against a monotone in-sample gain, S2039) while the tilt spans stayed perfectly monotone. One axis kept its shape out-of-sample and one did not. The tilt varies a free blend parameter and the untruncation varies table capacity -- but that distinction does not survive S2038, where the map cut, also a capacity change, reproduced almost exactly (-0.206 fresh against -0.236 in-sample). Capacity-versus-blend is not the explanation and none is claimed.

THE_TRANSFER_BOUNDARY_IS_BRACKETED_S2051.amplification_is_a_mechanism_not_just_a_: Both surviving steps GREW on fresh rows, 3.4x and 1.8x, rather than merely holding. A real effect measured on rows chosen for it is if anything under-estimated, which is the opposite of the fitted case.
THE_TRANSFER_BOUNDARY_IS_BRACKETED_S2051.claim: S1941's nn75m512 step beats the deployed design by +83.990 milli-nats on fresh rows at 5,419 (t = +23.41) and +73.843 at 16,110 (t = +25.00), against +24.400 in-sample -- 3.4x LARGER. S1959's endpoint still beats it by +43.899 and +24.925. The largest at-risk step of the build lineage amplifies rather than merely surviving.
THE_TRANSFER_BOUNDARY_IS_BRACKETED_S2051.evidence: ops/the_largest_lineage_step_on_fresh_rows.py, 193.9s, five arms on the fresh role at both coverages. All four predicates True, derived controls True, no crashed predicates.
THE_TRANSFER_BOUNDARY_IS_BRACKETED_S2051.open: The bracket [3.3, 24.4] can be halved by one arm. S1947's table-curve knee sits at 0.011 nats -- inside the gap -- and is the section S1947's price rule itself comes from, so it is both inside the gap and load-bearing.
THE_TRANSFER_BOUNDARY_IS_BRACKETED_S2051.the_transfer_boundary_bracketed: LESSON 106 set the at-risk threshold at about 30 milli-nats by argument. The measurements now bound it from both sides: S2018 +0.962 -> -10.371 REVERSED; S2020 +3.300 -> -11.578 REVERSED; S1941 +24.400 -> +83.990 AMPLIFIED 3.4x; S1970 +69.238 -> +127.889 AMPLIFIED 1.8x. Everything at or below 3.3 milli-nats in-sample reversed; everything at or above 24.4 amplified. The boundary lies in that gap and 30 was a guess that happens to sit inside it. Nothing in this ledger has been tested between 3.3 and 24.4.

THE_TWO_LAYERS_DO_DIFFERENT_JOBS_S1997.claim: The threshold's two layers are not doing the same job, and the asymmetry runs opposite to the registered prediction. Cutting ATTENTION 5's table from rank 384 to rank 16 costs 0.010/0.010/0.009 nats; the same cut at attention 6 costs 0.166 (S1996) -- attention 5 is 17x shallower. Removing attention 5 entirely costs 2.905 nats (1.971 -> 4.876). Attention 5 is PURE PRESENCE; attention 6 carries real, if small, content.
THE_TWO_LAYERS_DO_DIFFERENT_JOBS_S1997.evidence: ops/how_much_of_attention_five.py, 205.0s, nine arms x three roles at 5,419. pred_a True 3/3 (rank-384 reproduces S1992 to 0.005), pred_c True 3/3, pred_b FALSE. Derived controls True, both reference deviations 0.000000.
THE_TWO_LAYERS_DO_DIFFERENT_JOBS_S1997.open: If attention 5's requirement is presence with no content, the limit is measurable: S1983's meanrow null gives every token the same row, keeping zero information and only context-freeness. S1998 asks whether a mean row at attention 5 works as well as its rank-384 table, and whether the same null at attention 6 -- where content demonstrably matters -- does not.
THE_TWO_LAYERS_DO_DIFFERENT_JOBS_S1997.the_registered_prediction_was_backwards: pred_b registered that attention 5 would be STEEPER than attention 6 (>+0.166 for a rank-16 cut). It is 17x shallower at +0.010. Not close, and scored FALSE as written.

THRESHOLD_GAP_IS_NOT_A_FALLBACK_ARTEFACT.claim: The S1992/S1993 threshold's gap sits at COVERED inputs: omitting attention 6 from a compiled mlp2 costs 0.585/0.640/0.606 nats pooled, of which 0.558/0.600/0.548 -- 90-95% -- is at covered inputs, against a registered bar of 50%. The gap is strictly positive in all five target-frequency buckets, and the most frequent bucket carries 0.27-0.32 of the unseen bucket's gap against a bar of 0.25.
THRESHOLD_GAP_IS_NOT_A_FALLBACK_ARTEFACT.evidence: ops/where_the_threshold_gap_lives.py, 4.4s warm, five arms x three roles at 5,419, comparing mlp2+attention 5 against mlp2+attention 5,6 -- the same compiled MLP differing by exactly one attention layer. pred_a/b/c all True 3/3, derived controls True, all three reference deviations 0.000000.
THRESHOLD_GAP_IS_NOT_A_FALLBACK_ARTEFACT.open: A 3:1 frequency gradient looks like a mechanism, and after S1986, S1990 and S1992 that is exactly when to suspect it is generic. S1995 gives the full 36-site program's damage and both lone compiled MLPs the same bucket decomposition. If all compilation damage has this shape, the gradient says nothing about attention 6.
THRESHOLD_GAP_IS_NOT_A_FALLBACK_ARTEFACT.unregistered_observation: The gap is graded by target frequency, monotone on all three roles: 0.93 -> 0.75 -> 0.55 -> 0.42 -> 0.30. Omitting attention 6 costs three times as much on an unseen target as on a frequent one. Nothing was registered about the gradient; it is an observation.
THRESHOLD_GAP_IS_NOT_A_FALLBACK_ARTEFACT.why_it_matters: The uncovered arm is where the program guesses. If the threshold lived there it would be a fact about S1870's map rather than about the computation. The uncovered gap is larger (0.669/0.759/0.788) but carries about a quarter of the mass.

THRESHOLD_IS_DEFENSIBLE_LEVERS_ARE_NOT_E.alpha_is_not_a_spending_lever: mix10m512 and mix40m512 store the same rank-512 map and index -- identical cost, 178.9M both -- so the blend's alpha has no nats-per-100M at all (0/0). Alpha is a FREE parameter to be set at its optimum (S1943: 0.25), never traded against money. The first scoring left the resulting nan in the set and computed a median and max/min over it; both came out right only because Python's sorted() and max() do not propagate nan. Cost-neutral levers are now excluded explicitly and the exclusion is printed.
THRESHOLD_IS_DEFENSIBLE_LEVERS_ARE_NOT_E.claim: S1947's 0.010 nats/100M spending threshold, introduced as a round number and load-bearing for every allocation conclusion in S1947-S1957, sits INSIDE the measured exchange rate: the median marginal return across the priceable levers at S1957's operating point is 0.0143/0.0147/0.0090 nats per 100M. THRESHOLD_IS_DEFENSIBLE_LEVERS_ARE_NOT_E.evidence: ops/lever_exchange_rates.py, 4.8s warm. Nine builds x three roles at 5,419, each lever priced across its two neighbouring points. pred_a True, pred_b True 3/3, pred_c False 0/3, pred_d True.

The map is where marginal money should go AND the specific next map purchase is not worth its price, so the map's own curve turns over between rank 512 and 1024; where is unmeasured.
THRESHOLD_IS_DEFENSIBLE_LEVERS_ARE_NOT_E.status: CERTIFIED. pred_c's failure is the vindication -- I asked whether 0.010 was far from the natural rate and it is not.

_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.consequence: Every recovery figure for a fully-installed table+linear program (S1747-S1758) is the recovery of a PURE PER-TOKEN FUNCTION. The best of them, +0.78536 nats of a 4.2611-nat stake at table rank 64 with a rank-128 correction, is what a map from the current token alone achieves. The remaining gap is not program quality; it is the part of the model that is about other positions.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.does_not_apply_to: S1736-S1746, which are ablation and importance results on the LIVE model, and to any program whose substitute reads other positions.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.explains: S1747's -0.5462 joint composition failure (installing all 36 deletes attention, installing one does not); S1751's rank saturation (no rank helps a position-wise map represent something non-local); S1764's exact covered/uncovered partition; and why S1752's partial restoration of context made things worse rather than better.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.measured: With the 36-site program installed, a +10-per-channel poke at any position changes NO later position's loss -- exactly 0.000e+00, at both a covered and an uncovered poke site. The identical poke on the live model moves later covered positions by 1.184e-01 nats (S1765, ops/poke_in_program_context.py).
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.not_a_bigram_though: S1766: the program beats a bigram fitted on the same 24,576 fit tokens by 1.33 nats (6.57289 against 7.90729 covered CE, skip11000), and the plain table baseline beats it by 0.55. The tables are estimated from the MODEL's activations, so they inherit per-token knowledge the fit corpus does not contain. This is a floor on what the fit data supports, not a claim about lookup tables in general.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.purpose: Scope pointer, and the most important one for reading any table+linear program figure. Established by direct measurement at S1765 and derivable from the program's own form.
_COMPILED_PROGRAM_IS_POSITION_WISE.the_fact: Every site substitute in the table+linear class is `table[token_j] + f(x_j) W` -- a function of position j's own token and own residual. At layer 0 the residual is rmsnorm(wte(token_j)), a function of token j alone. So if every site at position j is substituted, by induction over layers the ENTIRE forward at position j is a function of token j alone. Attention is the model's only cross-position path and replacing its OUTPUT with a position-wise expression removes it. The program does not approximate attention badly; it deletes attention.

_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.CE_ONLY_SCOPE_S1788: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS ENTRY IS CROSS-ENTROPY. S1788 measured the settled standalone program with three other instruments on three roles: top-1 AGREEMENT with the live model 22.7-24.2%; top-1 ACCURACY against the true next token 13.55/14.25/13.64% against the live model's 39.32/42.35/38.88%, i.e. about ONE THIRD; and KL(live||program) 2.75-3.05, which equals the covered CE gap to within 1% (ratio 1.0010/1.0008/0.9912) so there is no hidden divergence off the data's support. DERIVED WITHOUT A FURTHER RUN, from S1782's bit-identity: at a covered position the full-rank program IS the length-1 model, so the CLASS REFERENCE keeps only 37.5/37.0/39.2% of the live model's top-1 accuracy. The accuracy deficit belongs to the class, not to this program, and context is worth about 25 percentage points of top-1 accuracy -- the accuracy-axis counterpart of 'context is at most 67.6% of the CE stake'. S1789 LOCATES THE DEFICIT: split by the TRUE TARGET's fit-row count, the program keeps 63.5/62.9/63.4% of live top-1 accuracy on targets seen 125+ times and 2.7/6.2/3.6% on targets never seen. The one-third aggregate is a MIXTURE of those regimes and describes neither. The concentration is the program's, not the task's: top-over-unseen accuracy ratio is 57.9/21.7/41.4x for the program against 2.4/2.2/2.4x for the live model, which is nearly flat across target frequency. 82% of the program's correct predictions come from the top bucket against 45% of the model's. Not circular - the program emits over the full 50304-wide head and is measured never to place the argmax on a rare token. S1790 QUALIFIES THE CLASS CLAIM ON THE ACCURACY AXIS: an eval-row leave-one-out bigram MATCHES the program on the 125+ bucket (program margin +1.74/+0.94/-0.93pp, failing a 1pp bar and NEGATIVE on skip1200) and BEATS it overall (15.97/16.63/18.00% vs 13.55/14.25/13.64%), while in CE the program beats the same object comfortably (6.573 vs 7.295, S1767). The program does beat the FAIR same-data bigram by +4.65/+5.18/+4.04pp overall, but the bigram's own fit-to-eval ESTIMATION gap is +7.07/+7.56/+8.40pp - larger than the program's entire advantage at every role - so the edge cannot be attributed to the architecture on this evidence. No CE figure is retracted; the reading changes. S1791 CORRECTS S1790's WORDING: the program is bigram-CLASS in accuracy, NOT bigram-identical in behaviour. Program-bigram top-1 agreement on the head is only 51.3/52.9/49.0%, far below a 70% bar; they disagree on about half of head positions. The program is nonetheless +11.0/+12.3/+9.2pp closer to the bigram than to the live model it was compiled from. Among head positions where they disagree and exactly one is right the program wins 54.0/52.1/48.2% - a coin flip - so S1790's overall deficit comes from the TAIL (10.1/24.1/10.2% of decided disagreements there), not from being wrong where it commits on the head. _CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.COMPILATION_IS_DIRECTIONAL_S1806: COMPILATION IS DIRECTIONAL (S1805/S1806). Top-down (depths 0..L live, rest compiled) is cheap and well behaved: half the 25.77/28.10/25.24pp gap needs 11 live layers, keeping the bottom four live buys only 2.2/2.2/1.7%, and compiling the top seven costs under half the gap. BOTTOM-UP IS CATASTROPHIC: compiling only layer 0 loses 62.6/60.4/61.9% of the gap against 4.8/4.4/3.7% for compiling only layer 17, and compiling layers 0-3 with 4-17 live is WORSE than compiling all eighteen (by 44.8/43.2/46.9%). Mechanism is S1804's: a compiled layer BENEATH live layers feeds them a context-free stream and they explode (live L5 emits 152x its row's norm). CONSEQUENCE: per-layer marginals from either curve are increments along an ordering, NOT layer attributions - the two directions disagree by two orders of magnitude about which layer matters (L7/L8 top-down vs L0 bottom-up). A targeted partial compile chosen by per-layer cost does not work: compiling all but L6-L9 scores -43.2/-42.5/-46.0%, worse than compiling everything.
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.COVERAGE_LEVER_PRICED_S1800: S1800 PRICES THE COVERAGE LEVER AND CLOSES IT. In the safe region (n/D 2.35-4.70, away from the n=D collapse of S1799) the curve is monotone but FLAT BY 3613 TYPES: equal +903-type steps buy +0.73/+0.76/+0.74pp, then +0.12/+0.20/+0.30, then +0.16/+0.21/+0.13 overall - a 4-5x decay, and on the head +2.80/+3.15/+2.67 falling to +0.25/+0.36/+0.25, roughly 10x. Extrapolating at the LAST marginal rate with NO further decay (an upper bound), covering the ENTIRE remaining vocabulary (44,838 types, 49.7 more steps) reaches at most 21.5/24.7/20.1% against live 39.3/42.4/38.9% - still short by ~18pp. So S1793's coverage-bound tail cannot be fixed by coverage. Together with S1796/S1797 (bigram complementarity real but unreachable from either arm's self-assessment) every lever inside the position-wise class is now priced and none reaches the model: the 25.8pp accuracy gap and the 2.88-nat CE gap are CONTEXT, which the class deletes by construction (S1765).
_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.DEEP_PREFIX_ONSET_AT_DEPTH1_S1829: The bottom-up recovery curve falls at LAYER 1, not layer 5. _CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.INTERFACE_GAIN_REMEDY_S1821: S1806's DIRECTIONAL POISONING HAS A ONE-NUMBER REMEDY (S1818-S1821). Holding a live attention layer above a compiled stream costs up to -12.4pp (S1802). S1818 traced 85% of L5's excess output norm to head 5.7, the S1089 constant-bias head. S1819 REFUTED the pattern-dispersal mechanism: 5.7 keeps writing the SAME fixed vector (cosine +0.9990, dispersion 0.0997 -> 0.3398) 159x too large, and compilation makes attention outputs MORE position-constant globally (median 3.06 -> 0.58 at L4). S1820 repaired the cliff with nine per-head scalars (-11.88pp -> -0.05pp) and found 5.7's 85% norm share is only 15% of the DAMAGE. S1821 then showed the nine were over-parameterised: ONE scalar per layer, the live-norm-weighted mean ratio (1/132.87 at L5, 1/63.04 at L6), recovers 99.7/98.4/99.6% and repairs L6 equally well. L5's vector applied at L6 still recovers 52.5%, confirming only overall SCALE matters. NOT a contradiction of S1810: site-level magnitude is irrelevant when everything downstream is a table and nearly sufficient when a live module must consume the output. SCOPED BY S1822: the one-scalar-per-layer remedy works ONLY where the live layer's input is the fully compiled stream the gain was measured in - i.e. the single-live-layer configuration of S1820/S1821. Applying the same gains across a bottom-up split FAILS: at B3 correcting only the interface layer makes it WORSE (-44.8% -> -48.7%), and at B0 correcting all live layers is actively harmful (+37.4% -> -4.1%), because layers above the interface see a progressively more live stream, are not inflated, and dividing them by 60-130x annihilates them. What survives: at B3 and B5 the all-layer correction still converts -44.8%/-43.9% into +10.3%/+11.5%, better than compiling all eighteen, so S1806's bottom-up direction is NOT structurally blocked - the correction simply has to be measured in the configuration it is used in. Sequential calibration (correct the interface layer, re-measure, correct the next, upward) is the best gain construction available and is best at every depth and role: B0 64.8/65.3/61.3% (vs 55.7 matched, -4.1 global, 37.4 raw). But at B3 it beats the better one-shot source by only +1.6/+1.6/+0.0 points against a 5-point bar - EXACTLY TIED on skip1200 - and recovers ~12% of the gap at B3/B5. So the deep-prefix residual (~88%) is NOT a scale error and no per-layer scalar will reach it. The single-interface case and the deep-prefix case are DIFFERENT PROBLEMS and only the first is a gain problem. Known-answer check passed: the first sequential gain equals the global gain at every depth (0.1693 vs 0.1696 at B3), forced because the interface layer sees the fully compiled stream under both constructions.

_CONTEXT_FREE_TABLE_FRONTIER.RIDGE_SCOPE_S1803: RIDGE SCOPE (S1799/S1801/S1803). The rank-64 embedding->row map's ridge is set as an ABSOLUTE 0.01*(n/D), which measures 1.38e-09 * lambda_max(Ecov^T Ecov) -- inert. At FULL coverage this costs almost nothing (best scaled ridge 0.1*lmax gains only +0.26/+0.11/+0.18pp, 0.4-1.0% of the gap) because cond(A)=324 there and the data term conditions the solve on its own. But BELOW n ~ 2D it is catastrophic: at n=D=1152 the inert ridge scores 2.40/2.51/2.28% against 11.84/12.39/11.72% for 0.1*lmax, a 9.4-9.9pp collapse. Every accuracy figure in S1788-S1802 was measured at full coverage and is therefore within 0.26pp of the best ridge in this family. The design point stands; the ridge is close to optimal AT FULL COVERAGE ONLY and must not be reused at lower coverage without rescaling to lambda_max.

_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.CE_ONLY_SCOPE_S1788: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS ENTRY IS CROSS-ENTROPY. S1788 measured the settled standalone program with three other instruments on three roles: top-1 AGREEMENT with the live model 22.7-24.2%; top-1 ACCURACY against the true next token 13.55/14.25/13.64% against the live model's 39.32/42.35/38.88%, i.e. about ONE THIRD; and KL(live||program) 2.75-3.05, which equals the covered CE gap to within 1% (ratio 1.0010/1.0008/0.9912) so there is no hidden divergence off the data's support. 'Recovers 32.4% of the stake' and 'keeps a third of the model's next-token accuracy' are different sentences; quote both. DERIVED WITHOUT A FURTHER RUN, from S1782's bit-identity: at a covered position the full-rank program IS the length-1 model, so the CLASS REFERENCE keeps only 37.5/37.0/39.2% of the live model's top-1 accuracy. The accuracy deficit belongs to the class, not to this program, and context is worth about 25 percentage points of top-1 accuracy -- the accuracy-axis counterpart of 'context is at most 67.6% of the CE stake'. S1789 LOCATES THE DEFICIT: split by the TRUE TARGET's fit-row count, the program keeps 63.5/62.9/63.4% of live top-1 accuracy on targets seen 125+ times and 2.7/6.2/3.6% on targets never seen. The one-third aggregate is a MIXTURE of those regimes and describes neither. The concentration is the program's, not the task's: top-over-unseen accuracy ratio is 57.9/21.7/41.4x for the program against 2.4/2.2/2.4x for the live model, which is nearly flat across target frequency. 82% of the program's correct predictions come from the top bucket against 45% of the model's. Not circular - the program emits over the full 50304-wide head and is measured never to place the argmax on a rare token. S1790 QUALIFIES THE CLASS CLAIM ON THE ACCURACY AXIS: an eval-row leave-one-out bigram MATCHES the program on the 125+ bucket (program margin +1.74/+0.94/-0.93pp, failing a 1pp bar and NEGATIVE on skip1200) and BEATS it overall (15.97/16.63/18.00% vs 13.55/14.25/13.64%), while in CE the program beats the same object comfortably (6.573 vs 7.295, S1767). The program does beat the FAIR same-data bigram by +4.65/+5.18/+4.04pp overall, but the bigram's own fit-to-eval ESTIMATION gap is +7.07/+7.56/+8.40pp - larger than the program's entire advantage at every role - so the edge cannot be attributed to the architecture on this evidence. No CE figure is retracted; the reading changes. S1791 CORRECTS S1790's WORDING: the program is bigram-CLASS in accuracy, NOT bigram-identical in behaviour. Program-bigram top-1 agreement on the head is only 51.3/52.9/49.0%, far below a 70% bar; they disagree on about half of head positions. The program is nonetheless +11.0/+12.3/+9.2pp closer to the bigram than to the live model it was compiled from. Among head positions where they disagree and exactly one is right the program wins 54.0/52.1/48.2% - a coin flip - so S1790's overall deficit comes from the TAIL (10.1/24.1/10.2% of decided disagreements there), not from being wrong where it commits on the head. An oracle union of the two reaches 49.1/50.9/52.0% on the head, +10 to +12pp over either alone and still 9-12pp below live: they are substantially complementary. S1793 DISENTANGLES S1789's CONFOUND: matched on HELD-OUT frequency (leave-one-role-out) and differing only in fit coverage, the program scores 0.45/0.45/0.00% on frequent-but-uncovered targets (n 447/443/234) against 39.01/40.42/38.91% on frequent-and-covered ones, while the live model moves only 30.65/32.96/27.35% -> 61.46/64.31/61.37%. The program's limit on the tail is COVERAGE, not frequency: targets absent from the 5419-type fit set are unreachable. All four predictions passed including the cross-run control on S1789's published accuracies.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.COMPILATION_IS_DIRECTIONAL_S1806: COMPILATION IS DIRECTIONAL (S1805/S1806). Top-down (depths 0..L live, rest compiled) is cheap and well behaved: half the 25.77/28.10/25.24pp gap needs 11 live layers, keeping the bottom four live buys only 2.2/2.2/1.7%, and compiling the top seven costs under half the gap. BOTTOM-UP IS CATASTROPHIC: compiling only layer 0 loses 62.6/60.4/61.9% of the gap against 4.8/4.4/3.7% for compiling only layer 17, and compiling layers 0-3 with 4-17 live is WORSE than compiling all eighteen (by 44.8/43.2/46.9%). Mechanism is S1804's: a compiled layer BENEATH live layers feeds them a context-free stream and they explode (live L5 emits 152x its row's norm). CONSEQUENCE: per-layer marginals from either curve are increments along an ordering, NOT layer attributions - the two directions disagree by two orders of magnitude about which layer matters (L7/L8 top-down vs L0 bottom-up). A targeted partial compile chosen by per-layer cost does not work: compiling all but L6-L9 scores -43.2/-42.5/-46.0%, worse than compiling everything.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.CORRECTED_2026_08_28_CODEX_RED_TEAM: This entry originally called 5.97902 THE CEILING of the position-wise class. That is not licensed. For the class of all position-wise predictors g(t_j) the CE optimum is the true conditional P(t_{j+1}|t_j), i.e. H(T_{j+1}|T_j); the length-1 transformer output is ONE FEASIBLE member of the class, not its optimum. Because it is achievable, its CE is an UPPER bound on the class optimum, so the bounds run the other way: the class reaches AT LEAST 32.4% of the stake, and context is AT MOST 67.6%. The 'unclaimed 43%' figure is void -- S1769's context-free tables reach this reference exactly and the distance to the true optimum is unknown. Quantifying it needs a defensible estimate of H(T_{j+1}|T_j), which S1767 showed these row budgets cannot supply.

Per-head decomposition through c_proj, live vs fully-compiled stream, skip7000: h7 carries 85.0% of L5's excess output norm (h2 10%, h6 3%, rest <=1%), going 6657.8 -> 1057986.8 (158.9x). _POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.INTERFACE_GAIN_REMEDY_S1821: S1806's DIRECTIONAL POISONING HAS A ONE-NUMBER REMEDY (S1818-S1821). Holding a live attention layer above a compiled stream costs up to -12.4pp (S1802). S1818 traced 85% of L5's excess output norm to head 5.7, the S1089 constant-bias head. S1819 REFUTED the pattern-dispersal mechanism: 5.7 keeps writing the SAME fixed vector (cosine +0.9990, dispersion 0.0997 -> 0.3398) 159x too large, and compilation makes attention outputs MORE position-constant globally (median 3.06 -> 0.58 at L4). S1820 repaired the cliff with nine per-head scalars (-11.88pp -> -0.05pp) and found 5.7's 85% norm share is only 15% of the DAMAGE. S1821 then showed the nine were over-parameterised: ONE scalar per layer, the live-norm-weighted mean ratio (1/132.87 at L5, 1/63.04 at L6), recovers 99.7/98.4/99.6% and repairs L6 equally well. L5's vector applied at L6 still recovers 52.5%, confirming only overall SCALE matters. NOT a contradiction of S1810: site-level magnitude is irrelevant when everything downstream is a table and nearly sufficient when a live module must consume the output. SCOPED BY S1822: the one-scalar-per-layer remedy works ONLY where the live layer's input is the fully compiled stream the gain was measured in - i.e. the single-live-layer configuration of S1820/S1821. Applying the same gains across a bottom-up split FAILS: at B3 correcting only the interface layer makes it WORSE (-44.8% -> -48.7%), and at B0 correcting all live layers is actively harmful (+37.4% -> -4.1%), because layers above the interface see a progressively more live stream, are not inflated, and dividing them by 60-130x annihilates them. What survives: at B3 and B5 the all-layer correction still converts -44.8%/-43.9% into +10.3%/+11.5%, better than compiling all eighteen, so S1806's bottom-up direction is NOT structurally blocked - the correction simply has to be measured in the configuration it is used in. S1822's raw arms reproduce S1806's published full-rank gap fractions exactly (37.4/-44.8/-43.9 vs 0.3742/-0.4484/-0.4391). S1824 CLOSES THE MAGNITUDE ACCOUNT FOR BOTTOM-UP COMPILATION. Sequential calibration (correct the interface layer, re-measure, correct the next, upward) is the best gain construction available and is best at every depth and role: B0 64.8/65.3/61.3% (vs 55.7 matched, -4.1 global, 37.4 raw). But at B3 it beats the better one-shot source by only +1.6/+1.6/+0.0 points against a 5-point bar - EXACTLY TIED on skip1200 - and recovers ~12% of the gap at B3/B5. So the deep-prefix residual (~88%) is NOT a scale error and no per-layer scalar will reach it. The single-interface case and the deep-prefix case are DIFFERENT PROBLEMS and only the first is a gain problem. Known-answer check passed: the first sequential gain equals the global gain at every depth (0.1693 vs 0.1696 at B3), forced because the interface layer sees the fully compiled stream under both constructions.

The operative rule is 'spend the budget on RANK at any coverage above ~14k types', not 'largest coverage you can build'. Operative rule: spend the budget on RANK at any coverage above ~12k types. CAVEAT: all iso-cost figures are at the single 230.087M budget; S1853 found the coverage term changes sign at low rank, so the rule is not yet known to hold at smaller budgets. *** BUDGET-DEPENDENT (S1864) *** The rule above is measured at 230.087M and DOES NOT TRANSFER. On the 65.950M line (the cost of S1849's rank-256@5,419 build, all-position CE 6.06004 / 6.03311 / 6.04238), moving to 16,110 types forces rank 97 and COSTS 0.04437 / 0.03059 / 0.02214 nats; 9,054 types at rank 164 is a tie (-0.00482 / +0.00537 / +0.00364). Coverage is worth buying only while the budget still affords enough rank to use it; the threshold rank for the 5,419->16,110 step is between 97 and 361. ALWAYS quote the budget with the rule. RIDGE BRACKETED (S1865): the 5,419->16,110 coverage step measured on three iso-cost lines -- 65.950M (rank 97 at 16,110): -0.04437/-0.03059/-0.02214; 129.678M (rank 200): +0.01013/+0.02715/+0.02975; 230.087M (rank 361): +0.05568/+0.07911/+0.07395. The coverage term crosses zero between rank 97 and rank 200 and grows monotonically thereafter. OPERATIVE SCOPE: spend the budget on rank at any coverage above ~12,000 types, valid wherever the budget affords rank >= 200 at that coverage. 97 < r* < 200 is a BRACKET, not a location; one further bisection near rank 145 (budget ~95M) would halve it.
