SCOPING from S1849/S1851: the RANK ladder is coverage-specific -- rank-64 CE above the ceiling is +0.223/+0.233/+0.198 at 5,419 types and +0.278/+0.297/+0.253 at 16,110 -- so only the full-rank endpoint is general. S1849 also corrected S1848's attribution: rank accounts for ~41%, not all, of S1768's published 0.54-nat gap (settled rank-64 is +0.223 above the ceiling, S1768's rank-64+corr-128 was +0.540); the remainder is that build's fallback and corrections.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.RETRACTED_S1790_SEE_S1795: S1790 IS RETRACTED (2026-08-28, by S1794/S1795). Its leave-one-out bigram was held on the target by a '>=' tie-break: 30.4/30.6/41.1% of its hits were positions where the target was its own top-1 and, after the decrement, merely TIED the runner-up. The arm was inflated by +3.52/+3.75/+5.75pp. LEAK-FREE THE PROGRAM WINS: on the head by +6.19/+5.13/+5.69pp (39.01/40.42/38.91% vs 32.83/35.29/33.23%) and overall by +1.11/+1.37/+1.39pp (13.55/14.25/13.64% vs 12.44/12.88/12.25%). S1790's caution that the program's edge 'cannot be attributed to the architecture' ALSO REVERSES: the bigram's fit-to-eval estimation gap is +3.54/+3.81/+2.65pp, SMALLER than the program's +4.65/+5.18/+4.04pp advantage over the fair fit-row bigram, at every role. S1791's agreement figures (head P<->B 51.30/53.21/49.51%) and S1790's fit-row-bigram arm are UNTOUCHED by the leak. S1791's 'coin flip' on decided disagreements becomes a 65.38/62.36/62.42% program win. The earlier S1790 text in this entry's CE_ONLY_SCOPE_S1788 field is superseded by this note. S1796 CORRECTS S1791's ORACLE UNION (it used the leaked bigram): leak-free the head union is 45.97/48.22/47.52%, a headroom of +6.96/+7.80/+8.61pp over the better arm, not +10.05/+10.49/+12.19, and it sits 15.5/16.1/13.9pp below live. S1796 also establishes that NONE of that headroom is reachable from the program's own confidence: selecting a logit-margin threshold on skip7000 chose tau=0 (never defer), deferring on the least-confident 32% of positions already costs accuracy, and the held-out gain is exactly +0.00pp. The program is better than the bigram even on its own least-confident third.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.RIDGE_SCOPE_S1803: RIDGE SCOPE (S1799/S1801/S1803). The rank-64 embedding->row map's ridge is set as an ABSOLUTE 0.01*(n/D), which measures 1.38e-09 * lambda_max(Ecov^T Ecov) -- inert. At FULL coverage this costs almost nothing (best scaled ridge 0.1*lmax gains only +0.26/+0.11/+0.18pp, 0.4-1.0% of the gap) because cond(A)=324 there and the data term conditions the solve on its own. But BELOW n ~ 2D it is catastrophic: at n=D=1152 the inert ridge scores 2.40/2.51/2.28% against 11.84/12.39/11.72% for 0.1*lmax, a 9.4-9.9pp collapse. Every accuracy figure in S1788-S1802 was measured at full coverage and is therefore within 0.26pp of the best ridge in this family. The design point stands; the ridge is close to optimal AT FULL COVERAGE ONLY and must not be reused at lower coverage without rescaling to lambda_max.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.claim: The exact ceiling of the position-wise program class is the model's own output given only the current token, obtained by running each of the 5419 covered tokens as a LENGTH-1 sequence. It scores 5.97902 covered CE on skip11000 and 6.03465 on skip7000, against an all-tabled baseline of 7.35825 / 7.35114 and a live model at 3.09711 / 3.29205. On the 4.2611-nat and 4.0591-nat stakes this decomposes IDENTICALLY on both roles: the class can reach 32.4% of the stake, and 67.6% is CONTEXT that no position-wise program can touch.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.consequence_for_the_no_go: Codex's CONTEXTUAL_COMPILER_NO_GO_AND_GATE.md prunes the position-wise grammar on a correct derivation (S1765). This gives the prune its number: the dominant term is context at 67.6% of the stake and is genuinely unreachable -- AND 0.59387 nats, 43% of what the class CAN deliver, is still unclaimed by the best program in it. The prune is right about the dominant term and it is not free.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.construction: each covered token as a length-1 sequence; log-softmax over the FULL 50,304-wide head, since slicing to the tokenizer's 50,257 would change the normalisation and the CE. Zero lookup misses on both eval roles.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.position_caveat: there is no additive positional embedding and rotary cancels for a position attending only to itself, so a self-only forward is position-independent. RMSNorm and any length-dependent statistics are NOT ruled out by a length-1 batch, so this is the model's per-token function evaluated at position 0.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.protocol: covered positions from 64, coverage mask pinned to n96_skip80 (5419 of 50257), matching every published figure in S1747-S1758
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.what_it_is: a replicated SELF-ONLY REFERENCE: 5.97902 covered CE on skip11000 and 6.03465 on skip7000, achieved by the model's own output at sequence length one. Achievable, so an upper bound on the position-wise optimum's CE.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.what_survives_unchanged: the installed program has ZERO cross-position dependence (S1765, measured at exactly 0.000e+00 and derived by induction), so it cannot recover any contextual effect. That never depended on the ceiling framing.
_POSITION_WISE_CLASS_CEILING.why_this_is_a_ceiling_and_S1767's_was_no: The compiled program does NOT beat it (6.57289 against 5.97902). It DID beat S1767's leave-one-out bigram by 0.76 nats, because a bigram from 27k eval tokens is data-limited while the model's own per-token function is not. S1767's pred_c caught that and its pred_a/pred_b are withdrawn.

_SINGLE_SITE_REMOVAL_SCOPE.protocol: optimal-constant ablation, coverage mask pinned to n96_skip80, covered-position scoring from position 64, 2000 ROW-level bootstrap draws (NOT document-clustered -- S1701), float64 accumulation
_SINGLE_SITE_REMOVAL_SCOPE.purpose: Scope pointer. Many entries quote optimal-constant ablation figures. Those are ONE-AT-A-TIME removals unless the entry says otherwise, and S1736-S1739 established what that measure can and cannot support. Read this before ranking anything by a removal column.

what_is_established.and_the_ranking_carries_no_allocation_in: at a matched budget of 6 native sites of 36, the one-at-a-time ranking recovers 12.79% / 12.22% of the table-program stake against a random allocation's 12.48% / 12.10% median (S1739). It allocates like a coin flip. In program context the same ranking is near-INVERTED, Spearman -0.66 / -0.69 (S1738), and against leave-one-out it is uncorrelated, Spearman 0.026 / 0.011 (S1737).
what_is_established.composition_is_kind_dependent: The sum of the 18 one-at-a-time MLP removals is 2.361x the joint 18-MLP removal (95% CI 2.318-2.405, held out); for attention it is 0.399x (CI 0.383-0.416). MLP sites are REDUNDANT and attention sites are COOPERATIVE, so one-at-a-time ablation OVERSTATES an MLP site by ~2.4x and UNDERSTATES an attention site by ~2.5x relative to its stack.
what_is_established.not_a_coverage_artifact: a registered arm scored every position rather than only fit-covered ones and the asymmetry holds (2.325 / 0.347).
what_is_established.so_cross_kind_ranking_is_invalid: any table that ranks MLP sites against attention sites by individual removal compares two differently-scaled quantities. The scaling errs in OPPOSITE directions, so the distortion compounds.

_SINGLE_SITE_REMOVAL_SCOPE.what_is_still_fine: A one-at-a-time removal is a valid STAKE -- the CE cost of replacing that component with its optimal constant -- and every such figure in this registry is correct as that. The denominator of a ceiling is a stake, so ceilings computed against one are unaffected. What it is NOT is a measure of where a program's work is, or a basis for ranking sites of different kinds against each other.

_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.claim: Truncating the token term b to low rank buys the additive program +3.47 points at the small fit set with NO extra data (53.79% -> 57.26% at rank 8). Combined with the +5.29 points from 5x data (S1676), two opposite interventions confirm the deficit is estimation, not expressiveness.
_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.failed_prediction: pred_b predicted the regularised additive would overtake pure linear at this fit size; it does not (57.26% vs 58.17%). A token term at all 18 sites is not yet worth its estimation cost.
_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.measured_in_condition: MEASURED IN THE MLP-ONLY CONDITION (attention running real).
_additive_estimation_confirmed_by_trunca.shape: ranks 8-256 are flat within 0.4 points; only full rank collapses, by 3.5. The harm is concentrated in the tail directions estimated from a handful of token occurrences -- it is not a capacity trade-off with an optimum to tune.

_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.LEADING_HYPOTHESIS_NOT_A_FINDING: estimation, not expressiveness. The additive arm fits a per-token table at ALL 18 sites -- 6009x1152 parameters from 24576 fit positions, ~4 positions per token. At mlp0-2 the token determines the output (ceilings 90/96/77) so the estimator is sound; at the other fifteen sites b is near noise and W is then fitted on a noisy residual. Adding a term you cannot estimate is worse than omitting it. fit_size_scaling.py tests this at 5x data.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.RESOLVED_S1676: Hypothesis CONFIRMED with the coverage mask held fixed. From 96 to 480 fit rows the additive family gains +5.29 points, against linear +2.64 and pure table +0.21. Its small-data deficit was estimation, not expressiveness. At 480 rows: linear 60.81%, additive 59.08%, table@mlp0-2 57.16% -- and additive is closing at twice linear's rate, so the ordering is not settled.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.S1675_HYPOTHESIS_STILL_OPEN: The fit-size test is CONFOUNDED: the coverage mask is derived from the fit set, so 5x data took coverage from 5419 to 16110 tokens, simultaneously improving estimation and removing the hybrid policy's live-module crutch. Symptom: the LINEAR arm lost 3.29 points on 5x data, which no least-squares fit does. The offset control passed cleanly (<=0.56 points). SUGGESTIVE ONLY: at 480 rows the ordering inverts to table 56.50% > additive 55.02% > linear 54.88%, so the S1673 verdict may be specific to the small fit set. fit_size_fixed_mask.py pins the mask.
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.S1675_confound_quantified: the linear arm's -3.29 point 'loss' on 5x data becomes a +2.64 point gain once the mask is fixed -- a 5.9-point swing produced entirely by letting coverage grow with the fit set
_additive_family_loses_to_its_own_specia.claim: The additive program y = b(token) + xW scores 54.35% under matched coverage, BELOW both of its own special cases (all-linear 57.99%, tables-at-mlp0-2 57.29%). Coverage policy is worth 3.71-7.01 points and does not explain it.

The remaining ~30% is therefore NOT long-range structure a wider window would catch; it is outside any fixed-position description, i.e. content-dependent routing.
_attention_residue_is_content_routed_not.failed_prediction: pred_a predicted >=3 points from widening to lag 64 if the residue were long-range; it buys 2.03

_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.FAILED_PREDICTION_pred_a: Written as 'the smallest tested rank reaching 95% of full is BELOW 384, the value path's figure'. Routing's crossing is AT 384, so the prediction FAILS. The constant was also wrong: S1690's output shows the value path reaches only 94.97% at 384 against a 95.01% bar, so its crossing is 512. The corrected comparison (routing 384, values 512) favours the claim, but a failed prediction is not rescued by fixing its constant afterwards. Recorded as a FAIL.
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.claim: Under matched rank budgets on the same module (rank-r least-squares maps, data-weighted, compiled bottom-up), attention's ROUTING tolerates heavy compression while its VALUE path does not. At rank 64 of 1152 (5.6% of dims) routing keeps 62.82% of the write and values keep 2.37% -- a 60.45-point gap. The gap is 24.88 at rank 256 and closes by rank 512.
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.combined_picture: with S1687 (positional families saturate at 70.08%, so routing is worth the ~30% they cannot reach), attention's write is a cheap low-rank SELECTION over an expensive nearly-full-rank PAYLOAD
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.measured_in_condition: Each rank budget is applied to ONE projection group with the rest of the model running real -- a single-component statement, not a joint-program one.
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.resolves: the routing-versus-values question S1689 opened but could not answer in comparable units
_attention_routing_is_low_rank_values_ar.why_the_claim_survives: crossings are a bad statistic here -- both curves are steep near their knees so one grid step moves them. The matched-rank GAPS are the evidence: +60.45, +24.88, +2.10, +0.46 as rank grows, consistent and large wherever either curve is under saturation.

_attention_v1_path_stake.DEGENERATE_JOINT_ARM: the 'both' arm is identically the 'write only' arm: with all 18 attention output writes pinned to constants, v1 has no causal route to the logits (it enters only through later attention outputs). CEs agree to 5dp because they are the same computation. pred_b ('the paths are non-additive by >=10%') PASSED ON A STRUCTURAL IDENTITY, not evidence -- the LESSONS 29 shape, where a prediction about a RELATIONSHIP between arms is free when one arm is nested in the other.
_attention_v1_path_stake.NESTED_NOT_ADDITIVE: v1 is worth 0.7066 nats GIVEN a live write path and nothing without one. Combining the two numbers into a total for attention would double-count.
_attention_v1_path_stake.architectural_not_discovered: v1's influence is entirely mediated by the attention writes above it -- this follows from the wiring, like the S1662 correction
_attention_v1_path_stake.claim: Attention's threaded v1 path is worth 0.7066 nats under position-weighted mean ablation across all 18 modules, about a fifth of the residual write path's 3.5840 nats on the same protocol. First measurement of this path.
_attention_v1_path_stake.cross_reference_not_comparator: S1682 priced the write at 3.5570 under OPTIMAL-constant ablation; a mean constant is weaker so stakes here are larger (+0.027, expected direction and size)
_attention_v1_path_stake.not_answered: the redundancy/composition question the joint arm was meant to answer; no composition claim is made

_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.CORRECTION_S1690: S1689 read 'the value path is HIGH-RANK' off a single point at rank 256 that falls on the cliff edge. The filled-in curve (S1690, attn_value_rank_curve.py) shows a sharp knee at ~384 and fast saturation above 512. Two S1690 predictions failed in the direction of the model being MORE compressible than S1689 said. The supported statement is 'about a third of its dimensions', not 'high-rank'.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.NOT_ESTABLISHED: 'routing versus values' is not a clean contrast in this design -- the positional families constrain WHICH POSITIONS may be read while leaving the read full-rank; these arms constrain the RANK of what is read while leaving routing exact. Different budgets, so 2.37% vs 70.08% prices two incomparable restrictions and cannot support 'values matter more than routing'. The defensible reading is the rank curve alone.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.claim: Attention's value path needs about a THIRD of its dimensions and then saturates: with real routing held exactly fixed, a rank-r least-squares map at c_v gives 67.05% at rank 256, 94.97% at 384, 98.32% at 512, 99.71% at 768, 100.01% at full rank. There is a sharp knee between 256 and 384 (27.9 points over 128 dimensions).
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.claim_ORIGINAL_S1689: Holding bilin18's real attention routing exactly fixed and compressing only the value path (c_v output replaced by a rank-r least-squares map of x) is catastrophic: rank 256 of 1152 gives 67.05%, rank 64 gives 2.37%, rank 8 gives -26.10% (worse than replacing attention with a constant). Exact routing does not compensate for a compressed value path.
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.clean_routing_statement_from_the_other_d: S1687's positional families saturate at 70.08% with full-rank values and no routing, and exact routing with full-rank values is 100% by construction, so routing is worth the ~30% S1687 identified as content-routed
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.controls_S1690: rank 256 reproduces S1689's 67.05% exactly; identity arm 100.01%; curve monotone
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.failed_predictions: pred_a predicted rank-64 values with real routing would clear the best fixed-position family (70.08%) by >=10 points; it reaches 2.37%, i.e. 67.7 points BELOW a family that does no routing at all. pred_b also failed.

identity_check.note: c_v is LINEAR in x so the full-rank least-squares map recovers c_v itself; the 0.01% over is ridge-level numerical difference

_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.scope: hooking c_v also changes the v1 block 0 exports, since v1 is that same pre-mix v
_attention_value_path_is_high_rank.vs_MLP_side: S1664 found the front MLPs' token tables reach 92-98% at rank 64 of 1152; attention's value path needs 384 for the same fidelity -- six times the rank. Both are data-weighted rank budgets on a 1152-dimensional read inside a module, both compiled bottom-up, so the comparison is on comparable footing.

_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.TOTAL_GLASS_IS_NOT_AFFECTED: S1658 checked the benchmark headline series. As the ship improves its total effect shrinks (1.610 -> 1.176 -> 0.900) while compounding FALLS (1.43 -> 1.04 -> 0.80). The artifact pushes ratios UP as effects shrink, so the observed trend runs OPPOSITE to it and cannot be produced by it. v4 sub-additivity stands; the improvement was if anything MASKED. The confound is CONSERVATIVE here: equal compounding at a smaller total effect is a real gain, not a plateau.
_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.finding: S1657: joint/sum composition ratios track TOTAL EFFECT SIZE, not substitution family. Measured at four front MLPs, same rows, same cost definition: sum 2.55 -> ratio 1.03; sum 2.19 -> 1.15; sum 0.66 -> 2.14; sum 0.055 -> 2.16. At matched effect size a PROJECTION composed BETTER than a TABLE (1.029 vs 1.153), inverting the family distinction I had asserted.
_composition_ratios_are_effect_size_conf.mechanism: joint/sum has a denominator that shrinks faster than its numerator as individual effects get small, because the interaction term does not shrink proportionally. This follows from the ratio's algebra, so the DIRECTION is protocol-robust even though the magnitude is not.

_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.CATEGORY_WARNING: the rotated arm still RUNS the MLP and truncates its output; the linear/table/additive programs REPLACE the module. 94.87% is NOT a better program than the linear map's 58.17% -- it answers 'how much of the effect lives in k output directions', not 'how well can a program compute the output without the module'.
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.claim: bilin18's MLPs cannot be described by keeping a subset of their own 4608 bilinear features. Keeping the top 512 by std(h_j)*||Down[:,j]|| and pinning the rest to their means gives a whole-stack ceiling of -49.93% (worse than replacing every MLP with a constant), and the curve is non-monotone. A rotated basis is monotone and strong: 512 of 1152 output principal directions give 94.87%.
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.consequence: any account treating individual bilinear features as units of computation works in a basis where units cannot be removed, while 512 rotated directions capture 95% of the same output. For this model the interpretable decomposition is a subspace, not a feature list.

_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.measured_in_condition: Feature selection is applied at all 18 MLPs with ATTENTION RUNNING REAL; the identity checks are exact, but this is not a joint-program measurement.
_feature_basis_not_sparse_selectable.mechanism: the readout sums large cancelling contributions; removing either side of a cancelling pair does more damage than the pair was worth

HOW_THEY_COMPOSE_the_key_operational_fac.STATUS: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-27 by §1657. The family law asserted here does not survive a matched-effect-size test.
HOW_THEY_COMPOSE_the_key_operational_fac.measurements_that_still_stand: §546's 0.9666 at two blocks, §1656's 1.1530 at four MLPs, §541's 1.6 at six blocks, §1616's 8.9x at three modules -- all remain valid measurements AT THEIR OWN EFFECT SIZES. None of them licenses a family claim.

superseded_text.exact_restoration_is_strongly_superaddit: joint live MLP0+1+2 restoration .5115 nats vs .0573 singleton sum = 8.9x (§1616)
superseded_text.mechanism: §546: 'replacing a block with a table indexed on its OWN variable does not disturb the next block the way projecting its output does.' THE SUBSTITUTION FAMILY DETERMINES THE COMPOSITION LAW. Tables ~additive; projections superadditive; exact restoration strongly superadditive. These are not contradictory measurements of one quantity -- they are three families.
superseded_text.projections_do_not_compose: six blocks under rank truncation cost 1.6x their sum (§541), with cancellation in the increments (§543)
superseded_text.speculation_not_result: The table drift is ~+.19 per doubling over the ONE doubling measured (n=2 -> n=4). If it held to n=18 whole-model table substitution would be projection-like at ~1.5. One doubling does not establish a rate, and the front modules are not representative of the middle fourteen, which §1326 puts below the instrument's floor. TESTABLE, NOT TESTED.
superseded_text.tables_compose_additively: CORRECTED BY §1656 -- NOT strictly additive, and the label was mine not the measurement's. §546 at n=2 blocks: .6654 against a .6884 sum = 0.9666 (slightly SUBadditive). §1656 at n=4 MLPs (mlp0-3, each fitted against the real model): joint 2.52398 against a 2.18904 sum = 1.1530 (mildly SUPERadditive). Additivity DEGRADES with the number of substituted sites.
superseded_text.the_corrected_law: The substitution FAMILY still determines the composition law, but the right statement is RELATIVE not absolute: tables compose MUCH BETTER THAN PROJECTIONS AND DEGRADE MORE SLOWLY. Tables reach 1.153 at n=4; projections reach 1.6 at n=6 (§541); exact restoration reaches 8.9x at n=3 (§1616). Do not call tables 'additive'.

HOW_THEY_COMPOSE_the_key_operational_fac.what_is_actually_true: joint/sum tracks TOTAL EFFECT SIZE, not family. sum 2.55 -> 1.03; sum 2.19 -> 1.15; sum 0.66 -> 2.14; sum 0.055 -> 2.16. Large-effect substitutions compose near-additively; small-effect ones sit near 2.1 regardless of family, because the interaction term does not shrink with the individual terms. ANY composition ratio quoted without holding effect size fixed is reporting how big the individual effects happened to be.
HOW_THEY_COMPOSE_the_key_operational_fac.what_was_claimed: That the substitution FAMILY determines the composition law -- tables composing much better than projections and degrading more slowly (tables 1.153 at n=4 vs projections 1.6 at n=6).
HOW_THEY_COMPOSE_the_key_operational_fac.why_it_fell: That comparison was CROSS-PROTOCOL: my n=4-MLP table ratio against §541's n=6-BLOCK projection figure. §1657 measured projections at the SAME four sites, same rows, same cost definition. At the matched-cost rank the projection composes at 1.0294 against the table's 1.1530 -- BETTER, not worse. The distinction inverts.

_front_band_account.implications_for_a_bottom_up_compiler: 1. Target mlp1 first if the goal is nats: 6.997 against 2.19 for mlp0+mlp2+mlp3 combined. 2. Target mlp0 first if the goal is UNDERSTANDING: it is small, near the tokens, computes a 23-dim class code, and everything above reads it (mlp4 takes .674 dCE from mlp0, §1422). 3. Prefer TABLE-family components where composition matters -- they are the only family measured to compose additively, and refitting them against each other makes things WORSE not better. 4. Do not certify any front module in isolation: §1616's 8.9x superadditivity and §1485's mlp2 brittleness are both local!=composite failures at module grain. 5. A priced frontier already exists for mlp1 (.9624 @ 214 Mbit, §1480) and a cheap repair for mlp2 (1.8 Mbit recovers .80 CE, §1489) -- place new programs against these, not in a vacuum. PROTOCOL WARNING: ladder-protocol numbers throughout; §1324 warns they do not compare to exact-restoration denominators. Three incompatible mlp0 values exist. Never mix denominators.
_front_band_account.purpose: The bottom-up account of the EVALUABLE FRONT (mlp0-3) assembled 2026-08-27 on Logan's direction to go bottom-up from the beginning, quality first. The front is a token-dictionary cascade that thins out.

what_each_does.mlp1: the high-stake module and the MOST tableable (94.5%); its input edge from mlp0 is a ~32-direction bilinear channel that is 64% genuine signal against attention edges at 5% (§1463/§1473)
what_each_does.mlp2: brittle -- §1485 calls it 'the strongest local!=composite case at module grain': its plank is brittle in EVERY context. But §1489 shows a 1.8-Mbit CE-trained correction recovers .80 CE of the ship, so the brittleness is repairable at small price
what_each_does.mlp3: composes CHEAPLY -- §1496's 23-module ship (+.74 CE) has mlp3's output projection and mlp17's stream-reader both composing without incident

_front_band_tableability_ladder.CAVEAT_S1666_saturation: mlp1's 7.005-nat stake is a saturated measurement (CE 10.28 vs 10.82 uniform); read cross-module stake comparisons as ordinal. See _CE_saturation_caveat_on_stakes.
_front_band_tableability_ladder.claim: Live covered-position table ceilings across the evaluable front MLPs are NOT ordered by depth: mlp0 90.27%, mlp1 96.01%, mlp2 76.98%, mlp3 67.55%. mlp1 is the most tableable despite being deeper than mlp0.
_front_band_tableability_ladder.failed_hypothesis: pred_b (context share grows with depth) PASSED on its literal condition (mlp3-mlp0 = +22.7pts >= 5) but its motivating claim is FALSE: mlp1 breaks the ordering. Recorded so the prediction flag is not read as support for the generalisation.

instrument_check.hard_evidence: ce_table == ce_live to 5dp in every frozen arm

_front_band_tableability_ladder.limitation: frozen arms at mlp2/mlp3 replace 3-4 attention modules (CE 5.36/5.67 vs 3.28 live) and are damaged models; they serve only as the known-answer check. Only the live column describes bilin18.
_front_band_tableability_ladder.mlp1_anomaly: stake 7.005 nats = 8x each neighbour, AND the most tableable at 96.01%; its 3.99% residue is nonetheless the LARGEST absolute un-tableable quantity in the band at 0.279 nats
_front_band_tableability_ladder.protocol: per-token mean table, fit skip1200 / eval skip7000, positions>=64, HYBRID substitution (table only at covered positions, MLP live elsewhere), CE on covered positions only, optimal-constant ablation baseline

_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.claim: The front MLPs' per-token tables are low rank: rank 64 of 1152 recovers 96.5%/97.0%/91.7%/97.5% of the full-table ceiling at mlp0/1/2/3. The whole front band (9.25 nats of stake) is ~85% reproduced by four rank-64 lookup tables.
_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.mlp1_anomaly: mlp1 gets only 23.4% from rank 1 where the other three get 53-65%, and needs rank 16 for 88%. It is the most tableable front module and the least concentrated in a single direction.
_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.not_claimed: mlp3 at rank 128 scores 100.75% of its own full table; the plain reading is that truncation denoises rare-token means, and it is not evidence of anything
_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.protocol: per-token table, SVD centred on the position-weighted mean with rows scaled by sqrt(count) so truncation minimises POSITION-weighted error; S1661 hybrid substitution; covered-position scoring
_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.replicates: S780's effective rank 22.7 for mlp0 -- rank 23 reaches 89.24% of its full table. Also replicates all four S1662 full-table ceilings to the digit.
_front_band_tables_are_low_rank.supersedes: S1655 (discarded for an unweighted mean constant and a zero fallback); the corrected protocol moves the rank-23 figure from 85.9% to 89.2%, so the curve SHAPE survived those bugs even though the ceiling LEVELS did not

_front_is_tabular_middle_is_not.claim: With protocols matched (joint substitution, one grain, S1661 hybrid hook, covered-position scoring), the front four MLPs' joint per-token table ceiling is 76.45% and the middle twelve's is 21.73% -- a 54.7-point gap. The front band is a token lookup; the middle band is genuinely contextual.
_front_is_tabular_middle_is_not.corrects: S1665 compared a JOINT middle ceiling against PER-SITE front ceilings; this re-measures both as joint substitutions. The contrast survives the correction.

instrument_check.strongest_arm: all18 with every attention module in the model frozen

_front_is_tabular_middle_is_not.ratios_not_interpreted: joint/sum is 0.475 front / 4.261 middle / 1.708 late. This looks like a structural dichotomy and is NOT claimed as one: S1657 showed these ratios track total effect size, and the ordering here follows that confound exactly (sums 9.25/0.62/0.42). Ceilings are used for the comparison because they are normalised within their own condition.

_front_mlps_are_synergistic.FAILED_pred_a: predicted mlp1 would dominate (largest module by stake, highest table ceiling); it is THIRD at +1.00 against the other three's +3.96

MLP_only_does_not_predict_joint.note: residual nats (1-ceiling)*stake from the MLP-only condition rank mlp1 > mlp3 > mlp2 > mlp0; observed joint gains rank mlp2 > mlp3 > mlp1 > mlp0. Only the extremes keep their places. This is a quantitative test of the transfer failure _half_upgrades_do_not_transfer established qualitatively.
MLP_only_does_not_predict_joint.why_mlp1_displaced: S1666's saturation caveat -- mlp1's 7.005-nat stake sits at CE 10.28 against a 10.82 uniform ceiling and is ordinal at best; I used it inside a product anyway when writing pred_a

_front_mlps_are_synergistic.claim: Exempting the four front MLPs one at a time from the 36-site program buys +1.98 (mlp2), +1.62 (mlp3), +1.00 (mlp1), +0.36 (mlp0), summing to +4.97 -- against +7.53 for exempting the band as a whole. The band gain exceeds the sum of singles by 2.56 points (52%), so the front MLPs are strongly SYNERGISTIC, not decomposable.
_front_mlps_are_synergistic.controls: the no-exemption arm reproduces S1696's 55.04% exactly; all four gains positive; the largest CI excludes the smallest
_front_mlps_are_synergistic.intervals: 95% ROW-level cluster bootstrap, 2000 paired draws; NOT document-clustered
_front_mlps_are_synergistic.mechanism: leaving one front MLP real buys little because the other three still feed it their error; leaving all four real removes the front-band cascade. S1697's compounding seen from the opposite side -- there an UPGRADE to one half was attenuated by the other's error, here RESTORING one site is attenuated by its neighbours'.
_front_mlps_are_synergistic.not_a_contradiction_with_S1697: S1697 found half-level UPGRADES additive to within 0.13 points; S1704 finds site-level EXEMPTIONS super-additive by 52%. Different operations at different grains. Jointly: additivity cannot be assumed in either direction and must be measured per operation.

_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.claim: Upgrading one half at a time inside the joint 36-site condition gives +2.66 (attention) and +1.31 (MLP) over the simple program, summing to +3.97 against a both-upgraded +4.10 -- a 0.13-point gap. The upgrades are ADDITIVE; redundancy is not detectable. S1696's shortfall is COMPOUNDING: each half's upgrade is independently damped by the other half's residual error.
_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.consequence_for_pricing: attenuation is the tractable diagnosis: gains from independent work on the two halves can be SUMMED and then DISCOUNTED rather than being unpredictable. On this evidence the discount is ~4x for attention-side work and ~3x for MLP-side work.
_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.controls: simple arm reproduces S1694's 50.94% and the both arm S1696's 55.04%, both exactly
_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.failed_prediction: pred_a predicted strongly SUB-additive gains if redundancy dominated. The 0.13-point gap is an order of magnitude below the 7.7-point shortfall the mechanisms were competing to explain, so redundancy is not detectable.
_half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_n.resolves: the mechanism question left open by _half_upgrades_do_not_transfer

_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.PRACTICAL_CONSEQUENCE: half-ceilings measured with the other half real are not additive, not averageable, and not reliable even as DIRECTIONS of improvement at full scale. Budget allocated by improving one half's ceiling and assuming transfer will be over-optimistic by roughly a factor of three on this evidence.
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.RESOLVED_S1697: mechanism identified as COMPOUNDING, not redundancy: the two single-half upgrades sum to +3.97 against a joint +4.10 (0.13-point gap), so they are additive and each is independently damped. See _half_upgrade_shortfall_is_compounding_not_redundancy.
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.best_account_of_the_model: a compiled program of 18 token-or-linear maps and 18 four-position maps reproduces 3.065 of 5.568 nats (55.04%) of bilin18's 36 module output paths
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.claim: Upgrading each half of bilin18 to its best known family carries only about a third of the half-level gain into the whole-model program. The attention half gains 11.79 points alone (56.26 -> 68.05 under lags 1,2,4,8) and the MLP half up to 3.5 (tables at mlp0-2); the joint 36-site program gains 4.10 (50.94% -> 55.04%).
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.controls: all three exact -- baseline CE 3.29205 (S1695 assert), simple arm 50.94% reproducing S1694, joint stake 5.5684 reproducing S1694
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.failed_prediction: pred_a predicted >=8 points of the half-level upgrade would carry into the joint program; observed 4.10, a miss by 3.9 points
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.mechanism_unresolved: either the improved attention program's residual error still compounds through 18 MLP programs refit around it, or the wider lag set recovers information the MLP programs were already reconstructing from the stream so recovering it twice buys less. Both predict the observed shape; separating them needs an arm that upgrades one half at a time inside the joint condition, not run here.
_half_upgrades_do_not_transfer.scope: attention v1 passed through unchanged -- output paths, not whole modules

_joint_shortfall_by_band.FAILED_pred_b: Predicted the attention side would carry more shortfall than the MLP side, from S1697 where upgrading attention was worth +2.66 against MLP's +1.31. Observed the reverse: MLP 22.03, attention 15.95. The error is a category slip -- the value of UPGRADING a family says nothing about the TOTAL headroom at those sites. S1697 measures what a better family buys; S1703 measures what having any program at all costs.
_joint_shortfall_by_band.claim: Locating the 36-site program's 45-point shortfall by band (exempt one band, recompile the whole program): middle bands dominate the TOTALS (mlp_mid +12.52 [12.12,12.89], attn_mid +12.14 [11.38,12.98]) but only because they are 12 sites each. PER SITE the worst-modelled sites in the model are the FRONT MLPs at 1.883 points each and the best are the front attention writes at 0.150 -- a 12x spread the totals hide.
_joint_shortfall_by_band.controls: the no-exemption arm reproduces S1696's 55.04% exactly; all six gains positive; the largest band's CI excludes the smallest's
_joint_shortfall_by_band.gains_do_not_sum: the six gains total 38.00 against a 44.96 shortfall; each arm is a separate compilation, so these are six independent counterfactuals, not a decomposition. The 6.96-point difference is cross-arm non-additivity, reported rather than normalised away.
_joint_shortfall_by_band.intervals: 95% ROW-level cluster bootstrap, 2000 paired draws; NOT document-clustered
_joint_shortfall_by_band.transfers: S1668's MLP-middle bilinearity and S1688's attention-middle lag-1 failure BOTH transfer into the joint condition and land within 0.4 points of each other (CIs overlap, so they are not distinguishable)

_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.claim: A substitution fitted against the real model and applied jointly at many sites compounds off-distribution and past some number of sites returns a NEGATIVE ceiling (worse than constant ablation). 12 sites: 62.33%. 18 sites: -42.99%.
_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.diagnostic: non-monotonicity in the rank curve. The front band ran 30.1%, -9.0%, 9.8%, 12.3%, 52.6%, 68.7% -- a curve that dips below its own rank-1 value is reporting compounding, not dimensionality.
_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.prior_art: S546 found the opposite remedy also fails -- refitting block 1 against an already-substituted block 0 cost +1.0647 vs +0.6654 naive. Neither naive nor refitted composition is safe by default.
_joint_substitution_compounds_off_distri.usable_arms: the full-rank arm (no truncation error, isolates compounding alone) and single-band arms small enough to stay stable

_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.CONVERGENCE_with_mlp_side: the MLP middle band (mlp4-15) is the one a token table cannot describe (21.73% vs the front's 76.45%) and has the largest irreducibly-quadratic share (37.67%); the attention middle band (attn5-8) is where a lag-1 description fails worst. Two independent families, two different modules, same location: bilin18's front and back are cheap to describe and its middle is where the computation is.
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.claim: The lag-1 positional program's shortfall is CONCENTRATED in the middle attention band. Exempt-one (recompiled per exemption): attn5 +11.60% (26.53% of the 43.74-point shortfall) against a 5.56% uniform split; best described are attn17 +1.27%, attn15 +2.91%, attn0 +2.99%. Spread across layers is ~9x.
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.control: the no-exemption arm reproduces S1685's 56.26% exactly
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.failed_generalisation: pred_a (early attention best described, motivated by S843 placing previous-token writing at attn0) PASSED by 1.48 points on its literal condition but its story is refuted by the same run: attn17 and attn15 are better described than attn0. The pattern is middle-versus-ends, not early-versus-late. Fourth prediction in this arc to pass while its generalisation failed.
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.first_concentrated_result: after three diffuse-not-sparse findings (S1663 heads, S1671 sites, S1686 positions), attention's departure from a lag-1 description does have structure
_lag1_failure_is_middle_band.scope: attention OUTPUT WRITE only; v1 passed through unchanged

_late_attention_is_harmful_on_novel_targ.NOT_YET_INTERVALLED: the sign is reproduced on two eval sets but carries no bootstrap interval per site. Certified on two-set sign replication, not on a CI.
_late_attention_is_harmful_on_novel_targ.SCALE_stated: small sites. Total removal 0.007-0.030 nats against mlp1's 7.02. The SIGN is robust across both eval sets and all three sites; the QUANTITY is a few hundredths of a nat. A real effect at small scale, not a major pathway.
_late_attention_is_harmful_on_novel_targ.WITHDRAWN_2026_08_28: The novel cell was defined as not-seen-in-past AND not-selected-by-the-erroneous-future-induction-mask. It therefore was not the documented set of targets absent from context. The reported signs and specialization interpretation are invalid. The original values remain only as failure provenance and must not be used downstream.
_late_attention_is_harmful_on_novel_targ.claim: attn14, attn15 and attn16 have NEGATIVE per-token damage on `novel` targets on both eval sets -- replacing them with their optimal constant IMPROVES cross-entropy on targets absent from the context (-0.0100, -0.0022, -0.0148 nats/token held out) -- while costing on induction and repeat targets. Their TOTAL removal is positive at all three (+0.0301, +0.0071, +0.0159), so the sites are net useful and only their novel component is harmful. Specialisation for context-retrievable answers, invisible to any pooled-CE measurement.
_late_attention_is_harmful_on_novel_targ.protocol: optimal-constant ablation, coverage mask pinned to n96_skip80, covered-position scoring from position 64

_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.MECHANISM_UNRESOLVED_S1673: I asserted the mechanism was 'L2 weights directions that do not matter downstream'. That was untested. A simpler account: the greedy criterion was evaluated IN-SAMPLE on the fit rows, where a 6.9M-parameter table beats a 1.3M-parameter linear map by construction. The EMPIRICAL finding is unchanged (local in-sample selection is 3.5 points worse end-to-end than ignoring it); the mechanism is unresolved between these two and should not have been asserted.
_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.claim: Selecting each site's program family by how well it reconstructs that site's OWN output (position-weighted L2) picks tables at 14 of 18 sites and scores 53.78% end-to-end -- WORSE than using no tables at all (54.28%) and 3.5 points below the best assignment. Local reconstruction fidelity does not predict end-to-end usefulness.
_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.implication: any program search that scores candidates against their own module's output is selecting on the wrong quantity -- relevant to lattice/state selection done on local fidelity
_local_fidelity_selects_the_wrong_progra.mechanism: a token table captures each middle-band site's MEAN output well, which dominates L2, while the directions that matter downstream are ones L2 barely weights

_method_note: complementary discovery: cosine-normalized target attribution (output-defined circuits) + attention-to-source patterns (attention-defined); sink confound closed S1524. Selectivity > 50x requires NR=1920 verification (S1523).

_mid_band_feature_augmentation.CONTRADICTS_MY_OWN_DESIGN_ARGUMENT: The docstring argued augmentation should avoid S1679's cancellation problem because the linear map carries the bulk and features only correct it. True at k=64, FALSE at k=8, where eight features make the program significantly worse. S1679's mechanism carries over at low k: removing a handful of features from a readout that sums large cancelling contributions injects an imbalance the linear map must absorb, and eight do not pay for themselves. The curve is non-monotone in k at the low end -- the same signature S1679 reported for replacement (8 -> -34.68%, 32 -> -29.95%, 128 -> -49.62%); augmentation shifts the crossing down rather than removing it.
_mid_band_feature_augmentation.claim: Augmenting the linear maps at mlp4-15 with k of each module's OWN bilinear features raises the 36-site whole-model program from 55.04% to 55.80% at k=64 (gain +0.77 [+0.65,+0.89]) for 0.88M extra reals across twelve sites. At k=8 it HURTS significantly (-0.16 [-0.25,-0.07]).
_mid_band_feature_augmentation.controls: the k=0 arm reproduces S1696's 55.04% exactly; baseline CE 3.29205
_mid_band_feature_augmentation.does_not_reach_the_quadratic_remainder: S1703 puts the middle band's total shortfall at +12.52 points and S1668 puts 37.7% of the band beyond any linear map; 64 features recover 0.77 of the 12.52, about 6%. The band's irreducible content is not mostly 'a few missing bilinear features from the module's own basis'.
_mid_band_feature_augmentation.intervals: 95% ROW-level cluster bootstrap, 2000 paired draws; NOT document-clustered
_mid_band_feature_augmentation.open: k=64 is the largest tried and the gain is still climbing from the k=8 crossing; a k-sweep to 256/512 decides whether there is a path or a plateau
_mid_band_feature_augmentation.price: 0.074M extra reals per augmented site, 12 sites, ~3.7% on top of the linear program's 23.89M (S1680)

_mid_band_feature_ksweep.CORRECTS_S1709: S1709 concluded from the k=64 point alone that the band's content 'is not mostly a few missing bilinear features' and that the family 'barely touches it'. At k=512 it recovers 29.4% of the band shortfall. Generalising from one point on a curve that had not turned is the same error S1690 recorded when reading 'high-rank' off a point sitting on a cliff edge -- second occurrence.
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.FAILED_pred_c: predicted diminishing returns -- that the 64->512 step would be smaller than the earlier 8->64 step of +0.93. It is +2.91, three times larger. The family is still in its steep region at k=512 and the sweep has NOT found the shape. The docstring stated this consequence in advance.
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.FALSE_IDENTITY_CLAIM_CORRECTED_S1713: S1710 and the ksweep2 docstring claimed k=4608 carries a DERIVABLE known answer (least squares with all features recovers the module, so the program must equal S1703's 67.55%). It does not, for two independent reasons Codex identified in repair commit c564b0c8: the augmented map [x,h]W has NO INTERCEPT so Down_bias is not representable, and RIDGE=1e-3 shrinks even a representable solution. The ridge k=4608 arm is EMPIRICAL, not an identity. Their fix adds a separate arm constructing the exact native map Down(Left(x)*Right(x)) including bias inside the same compiler, which does have the derivable 67.55% target. SECOND OCCURRENCE of the error S1699 already corrected -- I reused the same ridge and added a missing intercept. The measured k-curve (+0.77/+2.34/+3.67) and the 58.71% headline are ridge-fitted empirical values and stand.
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.augmentation_vs_replacement: S1679 kept k features and PINNED the rest (replacement) and was -49.93% at k=512; augmentation at k=512 gives +3.67. NOT numerically comparable (S1679 replaced all 18 MLPs in the MLP-only condition; this augments 12 middle sites inside the joint program) but the qualitative gap is large and the cancellation structure separates them.
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.claim: Augmenting the middle-band linear maps with k of each module's own bilinear features keeps climbing steeply: k=64 +0.77 [+0.65,+0.89], k=256 +2.34 [+2.21,+2.48], k=512 +3.67 [+3.51,+3.84], giving a new best whole-model program of 58.71%. At k=512 the augmentation recovers 29.4% of the middle band's +12.52-point shortfall.
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.controls: k=0 reproduces S1696's 55.04% exactly; k=64 replicates S1709's +0.77 to the digit; baseline CE 3.29205
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.identity_check_available: at k=4608 all features are retained and y = Down(h)+b is exactly linear in h, so least squares on [x, h_all] recovers the module exactly; the augmented program should then equal S1703's band-exempt ceiling of 67.55% -- a derivable known answer for the family construction
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.intervals: 95% ROW-level cluster bootstrap, 2000 paired draws; NOT document-clustered
_mid_band_feature_ksweep.price: 7.08M extra reals across 12 sites, ~30% on top of the linear program's 23.89M (S1680), for +3.67 points; the curve has not turned so the marginal price is not yet known

_mid_band_feature_price_curve.COMPRESSION_CLAIM_CORRECTED_S1720: S1718 called k=4608 'a ~5x compression of the modules'. At the corrected 3x cost it is 214.991M against the 430.00M modules -- 50.0%, a 2x compression, recovering 67.5% of their effect. S1714 divided by the base program, S1718 divided by the modules with a 3x-undercounted numerator; third pass over the same denominator.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.COST_CORRECTED_2026_08_28: The per-k extra-real figures were previously stated as 7.08 / 14.16 / 28.31 / 63.70M. Those were THREE TIMES TOO LOW: a zero-native-call feature computation needs the selected `Left` AND `Right` rows, not only the `Down` columns (Codex, S1718). Corrected to 21.234 / 42.467 / 84.935 / 191.103M, matching the ledger at S1718-S1720. The FIDELITY figures (29.4 / 44.6 / 66.6 / 99.9%) and the no-knee conclusion are unaffected -- a constant factor on the cost axis cannot change curvature.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.FAILED_pred_b: predicted the shape would bend. Successive steps are +3.675, +1.906, +2.759, +4.166 -- convex in log k, accelerating. No knee.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.IDENTITY_CHECK_PASSES_S1716: BIT-EXACT. With Down_bias restored, the constructed exact map at mlp4-15 and leaving mlp4-15 live give identical CE 5.098802047929132 in the same shared-object run; pooled and maximum per-row differences are ZERO and the corrected-arm replay is bit-identical, corresponding to 67.5533% against S1703's 67.553%. Two earlier attempts were invalid (S1713: no intercept + ridge, landed 0.009 from target; S1715: omitted Down_bias, landed 0.506 ABOVE target). The difference is categorical, not quantitative: a correct identity lands ON its target, not near it. Codex's construction and run.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.NO_COMPRESSION_RATIO_LICENSED_S1723: This entry previously carried a WRONG_DENOMINATOR_S1718 field claiming k=4608 is '87.59M = 20.4%, a ~5x COMPRESSION' of the 430.00M of modules. That is withdrawn twice over: the 87.59M numerator was 3x undercounted (above), and S1723 then withdrew ANY compression ratio, because 214.991M prices the 18-MLP linear base plus selected native factors for MLP4-15 and is NOT a complete zero-native-call replacement for all 36 modules. Dividing it by 430M establishes nothing. Neither the 5x nor the later 2x reading is licensed.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.claim: The middle band's quadratic content has NO low-rank shortcut in the module's own feature basis. Recovery is approximately proportional to features spent: k=512 recovers 29.4% of the band shortfall for 21.234M extra reals, k=1024 44.6% for 42.467M, k=2048 66.6% for 84.935M, k=4608 99.9% for 191.103M. Gains ACCELERATE in log k -- there is no knee.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.extends: S1679 (features not sparse-selectable) and S1692 (feature-forming path not low-rank compressible) -- the content is not merely hard to select or compress, it is genuinely distributed across the basis
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.k4608_is_nearly_tautological: at the full basis the linear map is handed the module's entire hidden state and re-derives its readout; recovering 99.9% there is close to definitional, and the price (2.7x the whole base program) says so. It is the module re-implemented, not a compression.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.ridge_arm_coincidence: my ridge k=4608 arm landed at 67.544%, 0.009 from the target. That was luck, not derivation -- the missing intercept and ridge COULD have made it miss. An empirical arm coinciding with a derivable value is not a known-answer check.
_mid_band_feature_price_curve.unaffected_by_the_withdrawal: the ridge k-curve (55.038/58.713/60.619/63.378/67.544), the price curve, the accelerating-gains result and S1709's k=8 negative are ridge-fitted empirical measurements that never rested on the identity arm

_middle_band_is_redundant_not_small.PENDING_protocol_match: the 21.73% joint ceiling is NOT yet comparable to the front band's 68-96% PER-SITE ceilings; band_joint_compare.py re-measures both as joint substitutions under one protocol
_middle_band_is_redundant_not_small.S1657_caution: the 4.26x ratio must NOT be compared against the front band's 1.15; composition ratios track total effect size
_middle_band_is_redundant_not_small.claim: The twelve middle MLPs (mlp4-15) are individually below the instrument's floor (stakes .026-.106 nats, sum 0.6208) but carry a JOINT optimal-constant stake of 2.6453 nats -- 4.26x their sum, and more than mlp0+mlp2+mlp3 combined. They were never small; they are redundant, and single-module ablation cannot see them.
_middle_band_is_redundant_not_small.method_consequence: single-component ablation under-finds redundant machinery; here by a factor of four. Any per-module importance ranking of this model understates the middle band accordingly.

coupling.reading: The early block is a COUPLED causal program: joint live MLP0+1+2 restoration gains .5115 nats against a singleton sum of .0573 -- 8.9x superadditive, and MLP2 FLIPS SIGN after upstream repair. mlp0 cannot be understood or compiled in isolation from mlp1/mlp2.

falsified.claim: The prose-content factorization at MLP0/1 is FALSIFIED by a local same-realization oracle; MLP2 is a regularizer sign, not a replacement.

_mlp0_dossier.implications_for_an_executable_compiler: 1. The target is bounded: mlp0's entire stake is .799 nats in the ladder protocol. 2. A TOKEN TABLE is an executable program (zero original-MLP calls) worth ~86% of it, and no compiled map earns credit unless it beats that baseline -- Codex's {N,P,E,Q,O} lattice has no table arm. 3. The real target is the .110-nat un-tableable residue, not the module. 4. Expect linear grammars to underperform: the class structure is 44% linearly predictable. 5. Do not compile mlp0 alone -- §1616's 8.9x superadditivity says the early block is coupled. PROTOCOL WARNING: these are LADDER-protocol numbers. Three incompatible mlp0 values exist (ladder stake .799, scoreboard benefit 2.195, exact-restoration-on-frozen-ship). §1324 warns they are 'not directly comparable'. Never mix denominators.
_mlp0_dossier.purpose: Everything the ledger establishes about mlp0 in one place, assembled 2026-08-27 for the bottom-up push. ASSEMBLED FROM EXISTING SECTIONS, NOT RE-MEASURED -- every line names its source and was verified by reading that section, after a duplicated run (LESSONS 26) showed that scattered results get re-run.

size_and_ceiling.reading: mlp0 is SMALL -- .799 nats against mlp1's 6.997 one block later, 8.8x. And it is largely TOKEN-TABLEABLE: 86.3% of that stake is reachable by a 50k per-token lookup, leaving .110 nats that no token-indexed function can produce.

what_it_computes.reading: mlp0 does NOT re-encode the token -- the embedding never leaves the residual stream. It computes the token's CLASS: ~360 distinct tokens collapse into a ~23-dim space, 6x below the embedding. And it does so NONLINEARLY -- that class structure is only 44% linearly predictable from the embedding it is computed from. STANDING PREDICTION: any affine/linear read of mlp0 caps out low. Codex's v1 affine compiler independently hit this (QNN +0.010, 11.2% of its oracle).

what_reads_it.reading: mlp4 reads the CLASS-CODE tier, not the token table. mlp0 is its dominant input at 1.8x mlp3.

what_the_residue_is_NOT.reading: The context residual is NOT previous-token: its share (.2068) is at or below its own null (.2115). A prev-token feature does not explain what the table cannot.

_mlp0_dossier_resolved.CORRECTION_S1662: The original wording claimed '100% of the residue is attn0's write' as an empirical attribution. It is not: attention is the only module that moves information across positions, so an MLP with its attention inputs frozen is token-deterministic BY CONSTRUCTION and its covered table is exact NECESSARILY. The frozen arm is an instrument check, not evidence of attribution. The empirical content is the live 90.27% split. WHICH attention delivers the residue is a real open question and is not answered here.
_mlp0_dossier_resolved.claim: mlp0 is 90.27% reproducible by a current-token lookup table in the running model (covered-position, hybrid-substitution protocol). The remaining 9.73% (0.083 nats) is cross-position information, which in a transformer necessarily arrives via attention.
_mlp0_dossier_resolved.claim_ORIGINAL: mlp0 is ~90% a current-token lookup table, and 100% of the remaining residue is context delivered by attn0. mlp0 computes no context-dependence of its own.

instrument_check.known_answer_derivation: attn0 frozen at a constant => residual stream below mlp0 is embedding+constant => mlp0 is position-wise deterministic in the current token => a covered table must be exact => ceiling must be 1.0

measurement.protocol: per-token mean table for mlp0, fit skip1200 / eval skip7000, positions>=64; HYBRID substitution (table only at covered positions, mlp0 LIVE elsewhere); CE scored on covered positions only; ablation baseline = optimal constant from opt_ablation_consts_all.pt

_mlp0_dossier_resolved.not_claimed: the 100% frozen ceiling is a CHECK, not a discovery -- with attn0 constant mlp0 is a token function by construction. The finding is the live arm's 90.27% and the fact that freezing one module accounts for the entire remainder.

already_priced.reading: mlp1 ALREADY HAS A PRICED FRONTIER. Any new compiled program for this site must be placed against .9624 @ 214 Mbit and the .975 max-fidelity point, not proposed in a vacuum.

_mlp1_dossier.implications_for_the_sequential_pipeline: 1. mlp1 is where the nats are -- 6.997 against mlp0's .799. A compiler that succeeds at site 0 and fails at site 1 has captured ~10% of the early-block stake. 2. It is MORE tableable than mlp0 (94.5%), so the token-table baseline is even harder to beat here. 3. A priced frontier already exists (.9624 @ 214 Mbit); place new programs against it. 4. The mlp0->mlp1 interface is rank-32 and 64% genuine -- a sequential program must carry that channel, and §1616's 8.9x superadditivity says it cannot be validated site-by-site in isolation. 5. Do NOT assume mlp0's class conditioning transfers: §1491 says selectivity is a site property. PROTOCOL WARNING: ladder-protocol numbers; not comparable to exact-restoration denominators (§1324).

its_input_edge.reading: The mlp0->mlp1 edge is a ~32-direction bilinear channel and 64% GENUINE SIGNAL, against attention edges at 5%. This is the cleanest inter-module channel found in the model, and it is exactly the interface a sequential MLP0-then-MLP1 compiler has to carry.

_mlp1_dossier.purpose: mlp1 assembled for the bottom-up walk, 2026-08-27. Codex's v21 pipeline goes MLP0 then MLP1 ('regenerate MLP1 fit/validation states under true Q0; then freeze true Q1'), so this is the next site they will need. ASSEMBLED FROM EXISTING SECTIONS, NOT RE-MEASURED (LESSONS 26).

selectivity_is_a_site_property.claim: mlp1's channel is NOT selective for mlp0's classes, and self-derived classes do not rescue it -- selectivity is a SITE property, not a method property. Front map: mlp0 4.3x > mlp2 1.9 > mlp3 1.4. So a class-conditioned program that works at mlp0 should NOT be assumed to transfer to mlp1.

why_mlp1_matters_most.next_largest_mlp: mlp0 at 0.799 -- mlp1 is 8.8x larger than any other MLP in the model
why_mlp1_matters_most.reading: mlp1 is THE high-stake MLP: 6.997 nats, more than every other MLP combined by the ladder's own table. And it is MORE token-tableable than mlp0, not less -- 94.5% against 86.3%. A 50k token lookup recovers ~6.6 of its 7 nats. The single largest simplification target in this model is also one of its most table-like.

_mlp_stack_damage_is_novel_concentrated.claim: Constant-ablating all 18 MLPs damages `induction` targets 0.843x as much per token as `novel` targets (95% CI 0.794-0.892, held-out skip11000); constant-ablating all 18 attention sites damages both alike at 0.974x (CI 0.891-1.059). Where the target is absent from the context there is nothing to route, so the weights are the only source and the MLP stack is what carries it.

_mlp_unit_membership.gate_naming: 2026-08-26: the mlp17 gates are NAMED axes - the-gate IS the determiner-prediction axis (token [ the] rank #1 of 50257 by unembedding alignment; class effect 1.57 std; AUC .922): self-inhibition on the class own axis. pronouns-gate = the she<->he gender contrast axis. Reflected he-state hedges to NEUTRAL referents (the/they/it), not she - asymmetric gender coding. S1589/S1590. Extraction-property tests for the question and pronoun circuits in flight.

_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.claim: Across four matched rank budgets in bilin18 (same fit, same bottom-up compilation, same currency), only attention's ROUTING tolerates compression. At rank 64 of 1152: attention routing +62.82%, attention values +2.37%, MLP readout (Down) -15.16%, MLP feature-forming (Left/Right) -52.88%. Left/Right is still -37.10% at rank 256.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.closes_loop_with_S1679: S1679 found the 4608 bilinear features are not sparse-SELECTABLE (top 512 pinned is worse than constant ablation, because the readout sums cancelling contributions); S1692 finds the same feature-forming path is not low-rank COMPRESSIBLE either. Two different compressions, two failures, same object.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.failed_prediction: pred_b predicted both MLP arms would clear 50% at rank 64 against attention's 2.37%, on the reading that attention's payload was unusually expensive. Both are NEGATIVE there. Attention's value path is the SECOND CHEAPEST of the four paths, not the expensive outlier -- this reverses the framing given in S1691.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.headline: a compact program can afford to approximate WHERE the model looks, but not WHAT it computes
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.measured_in_condition: Each rank budget is applied to ONE projection with the rest of the model running real. The ordering replicates held-out (S1693) but is a single-component statement; S1696/S1697/S1704 show single-component measurements do not straightforwardly predict behaviour inside a fully substituted program.
_only_attention_routing_is_compressible.negatives_are_measurements: both identity arms return exactly 100.00% and both curves are monotone in rank -- the LESSONS 28 diagnostic for distinguishing a real negative from compounding. The substituted models really are worse than constant-ablated ones.

_per_site_family_not_band_family.claim: Family choice is a PER-SITE property, not a band property. mlp0 and mlp1 want a token table (+1.73 and +1.24 points to the whole-stack program), mlp2 is indifferent (+0.04), and mlp3 actively does not (-1.00). _position_wise_masking_cannot_isolate.claim: In a transformer, excluding positions from a CE average does NOT isolate a position-wise substitution applied at those positions: the wrong values propagate upward and attention mixes them into the retained positions. Interventions must be restricted in the FORWARD PASS, not repaired in the score.
_position_wise_masking_cannot_isolate.evidence: on a quantity with an analytically known answer of 1.0: substitute-everywhere + mask-score gave 0.5583; substitute-only-where-valid gave 1.0000. A 44-point error.

_predictions_that_cannot_fail.check: before registering, name the specific observable result that would make the bar FALSE and confirm it is achievable under the run's own design
_predictions_that_cannot_fail.claim: Three registered predictions in this arc passed without testing anything, by three different mechanisms: a no-op made every relationship-between-arms claim trivially true (S1681); arms nested by construction made a non-additivity claim a structural identity (S1684); and a one-sided bar was cleared by the very sign it was meant to test (S1705).
_predictions_that_cannot_fail.common_structure: in each case the prediction was satisfiable WITHOUT the phenomenon being present -- a property of how the bar was written, invisible from the pass/fail line
_predictions_that_cannot_fail.not_a_reason_to_weaken_bars: all three were strict; strictness does not help when the quantity cannot move
_predictions_that_cannot_fail.why_defences_miss_it: registered predictions constrain the science and known-answer identity arms constrain the measurement, but neither asks whether the bar is reachable from the other side. A no-op gets the identity arm RIGHT; a nested arm computes honestly; a one-sided bar is arithmetically correct.

_priority_metric_validation.CORRECTED_2026-08-27: The original claim of 'INDEPENDENT confirmation' was TOO STRONG and is withdrawn. Codex's math red-team (board 05:24) is right on the decisive point: SHAPLEY CLOSURE IS AN IDENTITY, not evidence. Shapley values sum to the grand-coalition value by the efficiency axiom, so '-0.0670 + 0.7277 + 0.2120 = 0.8727' is arithmetic and I should not have cited it as part of the evidence.
_priority_metric_validation.caution_that_came_with_it: group effects are NOT additive and NOT monotone -- attention's Shapley effect is NEGATIVE (-0.0670), and ablating attention on top of mlp012+deep REDUCES damage by 9-29% in 6/6 cells (S1334 inversion). Consequence: any bill that SUMS per-group substitution costs overstates the total by ~33% (ALL3/sum-of-singles = .664-.772). Frontier entries must not be priced group-wise.
_priority_metric_validation.claim: SUPERSEDED -- see CORRECTED_2026-08-27. Retained verbatim above so the error and its correction are both legible.
_priority_metric_validation.convergence: priorities.md ranks mlp1 (.181), mlp0 (.062), mlp2 (.041) as targets 1-3 -- i.e. exactly mlp012. Two instruments built on different principles (per-component substitution fidelity vs group factorial ablation) return the same answer: the early MLPs own the remaining error.
_priority_metric_validation.evidence: Codex's ship_error_factorial (token-cell factorial over {attention, mlp012, deep}, 480 rows/split, discovery skip=7000 + heldout skip=11000) finds mlp012 the DOMINANT group in 6/6 token cells on BOTH splits. Exact weighted Shapley on heldout: attention -0.0670, MLP0-2 +0.7277, deep MLPs +0.2120, summing to 0.8727 = the full ship exactly.
_priority_metric_validation.independence_reassessed: Beyond Codex's point: the two instruments are not independent either. priorities.md ranks by delta_opt x (1 - best fidelity) -- the residual CE cost of substituting a component -- and the factorial measures the CE cost of substituting the deployed planks for a group. Those are close to the SAME quantity computed per-component vs per-group. Worse, the ship's planks were BUILT by targeting the priority board, so mlp012 carrying the residual error is partly a construction artifact: Codex notes the early planks were fit under the attention composite and the bundle includes incumbent MLP2 glue.
_priority_metric_validation.provisional_data: Codex's red-team also found factorial v1 bugs: the copy mask covers distances 2-65 rather than 1-64, and rare vocabularies were recomputed per split. TOKEN-CELL values (copy / novel_freq / novel_rare) are therefore PROVISIONAL. The global MLP0-2 allocation 0.7277 / 0.8727 is unaffected. The non-additivity and negative-attention findings rest on the global numbers and on the m+d vs ALL3 contrast, which survive; but any per-cell number quoted from S1608-era boards should be treated as provisional.
_priority_metric_validation.what_the_agreement_DOES_show: a coherence check, not a validation: per-component unexplained-CE estimates aggregate to the right group ranking EVEN THOUGH group effects are non-additive and one is negative. multiseed_null_methodology.CONTROL_MATCHING_RULE: A control must match the claim on CELL (S1634), on CLASS TYPE (S1637), and on CONFIGURATION -- (rank, TOP) (S1639). Matching on rank, TOP, rows, seeds and statistic is not sufficient; matching on six axes and missing one inverted a conclusion three separate times on 2026-08-27.
multiseed_null_methodology.CURRENCY_CORRECTION_HOLDS: S1645's fix -- score RELATIVE CE rise (rise / that class's own base CE) rather than absolute -- continues to hold. rho(n_positions, relative rise) is -.098 on set 1 and +.0000 on set 2, across classes spanning 97 to 7156 positions. The absolute-rise confound that dominated S1644 (rho -.580) does not return under the corrected currency.
multiseed_null_methodology.HARNESS_SELF_REPLICATION: The separation harness has reproduced itself exactly across independently written scripts five times: question@mlp11 17/60 (S1633 vs S1635), the@mlp11 gap -.0115 (S1630 vs S1636), pronouns@mlp17 60/60 and -.1320 (S1634 vs S1638), plus law_generality's fractions identical across two process launches. Determinism of the seeded design is established, so differences between sections are differences in CONFIGURATION, never in the instrument.
multiseed_null_methodology.LAW: IDENTITY (which components or heads carry the mass) is uninformative unless the fraction is measured. MAGNITUDE (how concentrated the mass is) is informative, but its margin is CELL-DEPENDENT and perfect separation is not the general case.
multiseed_null_methodology.NEW_OPEN_QUESTION: Why does CE rise depend on n_positions at rho -.58? Either rarer classes genuinely lose more from mean-ablation (real structure -- rarer classes carrying more idiosyncratic slice content) or CE estimated on 214 positions is simply noisier than on 3766 (estimation artifact). Distinguishing them needs matched-n subsampling: score every class at a common position count. That test would say something about the MODEL rather than about the statistic, which makes it worth more than the question it replaces.

multiseed_null_methodology.S1643_S1644_THE_BRIDGE_AND_ITS_REFUTATIO: DOES THE SEPARATION STATISTIC PREDICT ANYTHING CAUSAL? NO -- NOT BY THIS MEASURE. S1643 mean-ablated each class's own mlp11 rank-2 slice (forward_pre_hook replacing the slice coordinates of the MLP input with their global mean) and found 6/6 positive CE rise with rho(gap, CE rise) = +.657 -- flagged UNDERPOWERED at the time, exact permutation p = .0875 on n=6. S1644 re-ran at n=12 with gap and CE computed IN THE SAME RUN: rho collapses to +.0559 at permutation p = .434, and rho(n_positions, CE rise) = -.5804, TEN TIMES STRONGER than the signal. CE rise tracks how FEW positions a class has (question n=214 rise +.0753; by n=219 rise +.0434; period n=3766 rise +.0097), not its separation gap. `by` has the MOST NEGATIVE gap and the SECOND LARGEST rise, inverting the hypothesis. S1643's headline is WITHDRAWN.
multiseed_null_methodology.S1647_S1648_THE_EIGENVALUE_RATIO: THE ARC'S ONLY POSITIVE, AND IT IS NOT CERTIFIED. After S1644/S1646 killed every predictor of causal cost tested in-sample, the eigenvalue RATIO |lam1/lam2| of the class-projected quadratic -- computable from WEIGHTS ALONE, no rows, no forward passes, no 20-basis null -- was registered as a SINGLE hypothesis and tested on classes it was never fitted on. Set 1 (12 function words, S1647): rho +.6783, permutation p .019, 12/12 positive CE rise. Set 2 (12 TYPE-SPANNING classes, S1648): rho +.5105, p .094, 9/12 positive. POOLED (n=24, same pre-registered hypothesis, neither set used for selection): rho +.4157 at p .0452. Pooled rho sits BELOW both components because Spearman on the union re-ranks across sets whose CE-rise scales differ -- heterogeneity costs correlation while doubled n buys power.
multiseed_null_methodology.SCOREBOARD: Generalisations that died on their first independent test, 2026-08-27: S1627 (basis bias read as row-stable signal), S1631 (law from two hand-picked cells), S1632's attribution (certification confounded with site), S1633 (certification confounded with cell AND class type), S1635's monotone-depth hypothesis (actual shape U, then refuted entirely by cap), S1636's mlp11-minimum reconciliation (function-word-specific). SURVIVED: S1636's core measurement that function words bottom at mlp11 (4/4), which held because the test was designed before the claim. The pattern is invariant: a law induced from the cases that produced it survives exactly until the first genuinely independent cell.
multiseed_null_methodology.SLICE_CONSTRUCTION_LIMIT: The ablation cost VANISHES for very broad classes. In S1648: `cap` (7156 scored positions, 10735 vocabulary tokens) gives relative CE rise -.0008 and `digit` (1702 positions, 1691 tokens) gives +.00004. A rank-2 slice cannot carry much about a class spanning thousands of vocabulary items, so there is little for a mean-ablation to remove. This is a limit on the SLICE CONSTRUCTION, not on the ratio hypothesis, and it predicts the effect should vanish for any sufficiently broad class.
multiseed_null_methodology.THE_ASYMMETRY: The two published cells are genuinely asymmetric, each now tested against four same-subtype controls at its own cell with the same statistic, bases, rows and regime: question@mlp11 is the STRONGEST of five punctuation classes (gap 2.3x the next best); pronouns@mlp17 is the WEAKEST of five pronoun classes (gap 0.26x of ` I`). This matches the original scoring -- S1597 3-for-3, S1598 recorded as a failure of sparsity -- and is the first time either was tested against controls of its own kind.
multiseed_null_methodology.UNDERPOWERED_CORRELATION_PATTERN: THIRD OCCURRENCE IN THIS LEDGER. S1614: rho .6727 at p .0192 on 10 classes, called REAL AT POWER; S1616 got rho .0182 at p .9601 on 10 disjoint classes. S1643: rho .657 at p .0875 on 6 classes, explicitly flagged UNDERPOWERED; S1644 got rho .0559 at p .434 on 12. The flag is what made the second case a correction rather than a retraction. RULE: a rank correlation on fewer than ~15 points is a hypothesis, and it must carry an exact or sampled permutation p AND a scored confound control before it is reported as anything else.
multiseed_null_methodology.WHAT_SURVIVES_THE_BRIDGE: Mean-ablating a class's own mlp11 slice costs that class CE in 11 of 12 classes (`is` excepted at -.00257). That replicates and is solid. What does NOT survive is that the separation gap predicts how much. The statistic remains a description of where attribution mass concentrates, WITH NO DEMONSTRATED CAUSAL CONSEQUENCE. Any future use of it for circuit selection or prioritisation must establish that consequence first.
multiseed_null_methodology.WHY_S1647_IS_NOT_PROMOTED: CAUTION 1 IS UNDISCHARGED. S1647's rho .6783 at p .0186 on n=12 sits almost exactly on S1614's rho .6727 at p .0192 on n=10, which S1616 then refuted at rho .0182 / p .9601 on disjoint classes. The structural difference is real -- S1614 was IN-SAMPLE while S1647/S1648 are out-of-sample against a hypothesis registered before each run, which is the protection S1614 lacked -- but this ledger has been fooled at exactly this magnitude and scale before. Two pre-registered held-out sets are better evidence than S1614 ever had and are still not a certified result.
multiseed_null_methodology.answer: NO. A single random basis is a sample of size one and its bias is confounded with the mask and site it is applied to. Every null in S1612-S1627 used seed 1729 alone.

S1633 appeared to confirm that (site held fixed at mlp11: certified 60/60 vs five fresh classes at 17-47/60, margin 13). S1634 then ran the same test at the SECOND certified cell and it went 0-for-3: at mlp17 the fresh preposition ` at` TIES certified pronouns at 60/60 with 83% of its gap magnitude, the margin is 0, and the class ordering ANTI-correlates across the two sites (Spearman rho -.300). CERTIFICATION IS NOT WHAT DRIVES SEPARATION.

multiseed_null_methodology.what_actually_governs_separation: CLASS TYPE x SITE (S1635-S1637). Sweeping seven classes across mlp5/8/11/14/17 at rank-2 TOP-4 with 60 trials per cell shows the depth profile of separation depends on the KIND of token: FUNCTION WORDS bottom out at mlp11 (at 17, the 24, is 33, and 45 -- strict minima 4/4); PUNCTUATION peaks near it (period 58/60 at mlp11); CAPITALISED tokens rise MONOTONICALLY with depth (cap [37 39 52 54 59]). No single depth story holds -- S1635's 'non-monotonicity is general' is refuted by cap, and S1636's 'mlp11 is the separation minimum' holds only for function words.
